articleTitle: Homogenization Method Based on Cauer Ladder Network Representation of Unit Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a new homogenization method using the B-input Cauer ladder network (CLN) method to obtain a continued fraction expansion of a macroscopic complex permeability. Since the CLN method ensures obtaining the Cauer circuit with all positive constants, the proposed method is suitable for the time-domain analysis.

articleTitle: Macroscopic Modeling of Mn-Zn Ferrites Based on Analytical Dynamic Material Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: We propose a semi-analytical approach for modelling the macroscopic electromagnetic behavior of Mn-Zn ferrite cores while placed in both dielectric and magnetic settings. First, analytical material models are provided for calculating the effective parameters, i.e., complex resistivity and complex reluctivity by solving the electromagnetic fields in a single grain/boundary cell. Then, the effective parameters are used in 2-D finite element (FE) models for solving the full-wave electromagnetic field equation in a cross-section of a ferrite core placed in dielectric and magnetic settings. The simulated dielectric and magnetic impedances of disk-shaped and toroidal cores are validated against measurements.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Homogenization of Windings Using B-input Cauer Ladder Network Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a time-domain homogenization of windings using the B-input Cauer ladder network (CLN) method. First, the novel CLN procedure is presented to derive the equivalent circuit of a unit cell as the homogenized model of the winding. Then, the equivalent circuit is applied to finite-element analyses of a flat-wire inductor to verify the validity and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Combination of Extra Random Trees and Genetic Algorithm for Optimal Design of SPMSM for Robot Joints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a method that combines extra random trees technology (ERT) and genetic algorithm (GA) for optimal design of motor for robot joints. The target motor is a surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM), and the design goal is to increase average torque while reducing torque ripple, iron loss, and total harmonic distortion of phase back electromotive force (P-BEMF THD). The prediction accuracy of ERT was improved through hyperparameter tuning and its performance was verified through comparison with other machine learning techniques. The applicability of the proposed method was confirmed by deriving an optimal design of target motor with improved performance.

articleTitle: An Improved Multi-Objective GA for Low Frequency Metamaterial Unit Robust Optimization under Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Metamaterial (MM) is very promising in engineering application since it exhibits extraordinary physical properties that do not exist in nature. Nevertheless, the development of a MM still faces bottleneck problems such as to maximize negative permeability and ensure the robustness of the high permeability at the working frequency in engineering applications. To address the inefficiencies of existing multi-objective robust optimization methodologies in applications to MM designs, an improved multi-objective genetic algorithm and an adaptive response surface model are proposed. The numerical optimization results of a prototype MM unit have demonstrated the feasibility and merits of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Estimating Parameters of Synchronous Generator Using Sudden Three Phase Short Circuit Test
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper outlines a method for estimating the parameters of synchronous generators using sudden three phase short circuit test. The paper introduces the procedures for calculation of parameters and simulation of synchronous generator. This study is meant to serve as a basis for future research that will explore the utilization of these parameter estimation techniques in the context of generator modeling, specifically for addressing the needs of fault diagnosis in synchronous generator.

articleTitle: Study on Numerical Calculation Method of Magnetic Induction Heating of CF Dry Cloth Using Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a numerical calculation method that combines the numerical calculation method of the eddy current and magnetization based on the integral equations with the three-dimensional finite element method for thermal conduction has been proposed for the magnetic induction heating of CF dry cloth. The results obtained using the proposed method were compared with the experimental results.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of RC Snubber Circuit for GaN-Based Battery Formation Device With Switching Noise Coupling Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for implementing the design of a snubber circuit to address the switching noise coupling issue in Gallium Nitride (GaN)-based battery formation devices. The proposed snubber design serves as process to avoid voltage spike resulting from the parasitic inductance within the PCB loop, preventing its interference with the interleave switch and mitigating the risk of overvoltage in GaN switches. Utilizing the proposed snubber circuit design, a comparative experiment is conducted to demonstrate the improvements before and after snubber circuit design. The validation result shows enhancements for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$44.6\%$</tex> switching noise, overvoltage, and ringing reduction.

articleTitle: Novel Distributed Magnet Flux Modulation Machines With High Power Factor and Torque Density
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel distributed magnet flux modulation machine (DM-FMM) with a high power factor and high torque density is presented. Based on the flux modulation principle, a distributed stator magnet arrangement is proposed. This topology effectively reduces flux leakage. According to the finite element analysis (FEA) results, the power factor is 0.93 and the torque density reaches 30.9 kNm/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> at conventional current density. In addition, power factor performance is still impressive at twice the current overload.

articleTitle: New Winding Structure for VR Resolver for Robustness and Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a new winding structure of the Variable Reluctance (VR) resolver, and proposes the finite element method (FEM) using this and the eccentric fault diagnosis method through experimental characteristic analysis. When eccentric fault diagnosis is performed using the resolver using the new winding structure, it is possible to know where direction the eccentricity occurred. In addition, through the new winding structure, it has become more robust from fault against short circuit and open circuit.

articleTitle: Loss Calculation of Iron Core Under DC Bias and Harmonic Disturbance Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper combines the improved Tellinen model with the transient model of classical loss and excess loss to propose a calculation method for the core loss under DC bias and harmonic. Based on the magnetic property's measurement of oriented silicon steel material B30P100, the excess loss parameters were obtained, and the loss value was calculated when a second harmonic was present under DC bias condition. The reliability was substantiated through comparisons of the results with measured loss data. This methodological refinement not only advances the understanding of core loss in transformers but also offers a validated tool for predicting and managing loss conditions under different operating scenarios.

articleTitle: Field Distribution Study for Microwave Processing Plasma Uniformity Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Microwave plasma is a promising source for semiconductor plasma processing for its ability to produce a considerable amount of radicals. However, due to the short wavelength of microwaves (12.2 cm for 2.45 GHz), it is difficult to secure high plasma uniformity. To resolve this problem, a study of field distribution in the plasma chamber is necessary. This work presents the study of field distribution in the chamber by imposing a phase difference between the two microwave inputs. Furthermore, we investigated the influence of plasma density on the field distribution. Both the COMSOL simulations and experimental results show that the plasma uniformity could be enhanced by properly controlling the phase and density.

articleTitle: Magnetization Estimation for Permanent Magnet Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A new method for the nondestructive estimation of the magnetization distribution (MD) inside a permanent magnet, using a convolutional neural network, is proposed herein. The proposed method improves the estimation accuracy by 15.1% compared to the conventional method that uses a multi-layer perceptron. It achieves high accuracy in estimating the MD. Furthermore, the proposed method accurately predicts the MD from the measured magnetic flux density distribution.

articleTitle: Surrogate-Based Optimization of SMT Inductors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Parasitic electromagnetic (EM) effects within passive components are a critical problem in EMI filter applications, especially when specific filter specifications must be met. In this study, a surrogate model-based optimization methodology is proposed to determine the optimal internal geometry of a surface-mounted (SMT) ferrite bead to maximize the inductance of the device over a wide frequency range from 1 MHz to 1 GHz. Preliminary results show an improvement of the device behavior compared to the original design provided by the manufacturer over the entire frequency range of interest.

articleTitle: Efficiency Analysis of Delta Winding Connected BLDC Motor According to Occurrence of Circulating Current
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper studied the effect of circulating current generated in a surface-mounted synchronous motor (SPMSM) with delta winding on efficiency. In a delta-connected motor, when the 3nth component occurs in the phase basck electromotive force (BEMF), a circulating current that flows only inside the circuit occurs. This current causes additional joule losses and degenerate motor performance. In this paper, the 3nth component of the phase BEMF was reduced by chaging the shape of the permanent magnet of SPMSM, and the performance of the motor was compared. For this purpose, a six step dirve was used, and the loss was separated into copper loss and iron loss according to the torque and speed of the motor. At this time, copper loss was divided into loss due to the fundamental wave and the 3nth component of the phase current. Finally, an efficiency map according to torque and speed was presented, and the diifference in efficiency between the basic and improved models was analyzed. The performace of the prototype was verified by a dynamometer load test.

articleTitle: Self-Consistent Model of Low-Pressure Plasma Column Sustained by Electromagnetic Surface Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The electromagnetic fields in a plasma column sustained by a surface wave traveling along the plasma boundary are studied in a self-consistent model coupling Maxwell's equations in the frequency-domain to the transport equations for electron energy and particles (ions, electrons, metastable excited atoms) in a two-dimensional axially symmetric model. The results are applied to study the factors governing the axial density profile of the plasma. The focus is on verifying the assumption of negligibility of the axial transport of electron energy and particles, on which the classical theory of surface-wave columns is based.

articleTitle: Simulation of Thin Wires and Dielectric Bodies in Multilayered Medium Using FEBI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Multiscale problem exists in computational electromagnetic. In geophysical applications, the casing is very long and thin in the subsurface while the reservoir or the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sequestration body is large. Assuming the background subsurface is multilayered medium, the geophysical problems can be efficiently addressed by extending the finite-element boundary-integral method and applying the thin wire approximation. Multilayered anisotropic medium is also taken into consideration. Numerical examples show the proposed framework can achieve accurate results.

articleTitle: A Magnetic Planetary Gear Permanent Magnet Machine with Double Blades for Offshore Marine Current Generation System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a new magnetic planetary gear (MPG) permanent magnet (PM) machine (MPGPM) with double blades for marine current energy power generation. The proposed MPGPM combines the outer rotor PM machine and MPG to improve the torque density of the machine. This paper investigates the relationship between the gear ratio, the number of planetary gears, and the PM thickness with the performance of MPGPM. The corresponding torque transmission performance are effectively evaluated using the finite-element method.

articleTitle: AC Hysteresis Modeling of Grain-Oriented Silicon Steel Considering DC Hysteresis and Anomalous Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Highly accurate iron loss calculations are necessary to accurately predict the efficiency of electrical equipment. Currently, most iron loss calculations for electrical equipment only take initial magnetization curves into consideration. At the same time, it is thought that the accuracy of iron loss calculations can be improved by considering the DC hysteresis characteristics and eddy currents. Grain-oriented electrical steel sheets that allow easy magnetism in one direction are widely used as iron cores in static electrical equipment. This study considers the DC hysteresis, classical, and anomalous eddy current characteristics of grain-oriented electrical steel sheets. The AC symmetrical hysteresis loops can be better fitted by considering DC hysteresis, classical, and anomalous eddy current characteristics.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Design Process of Limited Angle Actuator for Wrist Applications of Industrial Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This research presents the design process of the wrist actuator of an industrial robot. Two different electromagnetic actuators with wide and limited angles are proposed that can substitute the hydraulic counterparts. The simulation process and the output characteristics are presented.

articleTitle: Study of Magnetostrictive Characteristics Based on Dynamic J-A Model under DC Bias
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The existence of DC bias will change the magnetostrictive properties of the electrical steel sheet (ESS), thus aggravating the vibration and noise of the transformer core. Based on the theory of magnetic domain and thermodynamics, the dynamic J-A model and the free energy model are combined to construct a dynamic magnetostriction model considering the grain-oriented ESS under DC bias. The parameters are extracted by particle swarm optimization algorithm (PSO). The correctness of the proposed model is verified by comparing the measured and calculated magnetostriction values. Finally, the finite element simulation model of the transformer is established, and the constructed mathematical model of magnetostriction is loaded to simulate the vibration of the transformer under DC bias.

articleTitle: 3D FE Analysis of Magnet Segmentation for Reducing the Eddy Current of Arc Linear Servo Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper analyzed the effects of magnet segmentation on the output characteristics of an arc-type linear servo motor. Compared to conventional design, the segmented magnet structure reduced the eddy current circulation area. The simulation results showed that the magnet segmentation reduced the eddy current losses and improved the cogging torque and thrust force ripple, improving the machine's efficiency. The analysis is done for two magnet segments in this paper and more than two segments will be analyzed in the future with the prototype experiment.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of SPMSM for Robot Joint using Least Square Boosting Assisted Multi Objective Opimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper least square boosting assisted multi objective optimization (LSBMOO) is proposed for the optimal design of surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) for robot joint. The LSBMOO combines machine learning with a multi objective function optimization algorithm to solve the problem of computational time and improve prediction performance of the meta-model. In the case of non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm-II (NSGA-II) and multi objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO), they indirectly fill the blank in the pareto front set through various methods because there is no process to predict the value of the objective function area. Therefore, these methods are required many function calls to find the pareto front set. To solve these problems, the proposed algorithm generates a meta-model and predicts the objective function value, which reduces the number of function calls by allowing the solution to be added directly to the pareto front set. The LSBMOO proved its superiority by comparing with NSGA-II and MOPSO. In the design part, the initial design was carried out using various design techniques, and design variables and objective functions are selected for linkage analysis with LSBMOO. The optimal design model is derived by extracting the pareto front set and selecting the optimal solution according to the importance of the objective function.

articleTitle: A Study on the Design of Novel Slotless Axial Flux Motor Through Comparison with Radial Flux Motor for Collaborative Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper shows a comparison of characteristics when designing a motor for a collaborative robot by changing PMSM (Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor) type from a slotless RFM (Radial Flux Motor) to AFM (Axial Flux Motor). First, RFM with a novel slotless coil is introduced. Constraints of novel slotless AFM for equivalent comparison are selected. The shape is determined based on the size equation of AFM and FEA (Finite Element Analysis) results to maximize power and efficiency within constraints. Finally, by comparing the characteristics of AFM and RFM through FEA, the advantages of applying AFM are confirmed.

articleTitle: Fast Computation of Steady-State Performance in Line-Start Synchronous Reluctance Motor Based on Equivalent Circuit and Finite Element Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Line-Start Synchronous Reluctance Motor (LSSynRM) has been received the attention as high efficiency motor. However, LS-SynRM must be performed using electromagnetic and mechanical transient analysis of finite-element analysis (FEA). This analysis method has a disadvantage of requiring a lot of analysis time. Therefore, in this paper, the fast performance analysis method is proposed based on an equivalent circuit and FEA. The operating points of LS-SynRM are determined by the dq-axis inductances which have the nonlinear characteristics. Considering the nonlinear characteristic of dq-axis inductance, the parameter is computed using magnetostatic FEA. Based on the motor parameters and equivalent circuit, the current vector is computed, and the iteration is performed until the current vector converges. By comparing the performances using the proposed analysis method and electromagnetic and mechanical transient analysis of FEA according to the load conditions, the effectiveness of the proposed analysis method is verified. Furthermore, the manufactured <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.2{{\ kW}}$</tex> LS-SynRM is testing, and the proposed analysis method is verified by comparing experiment results.

articleTitle: An AC Copper Loss Calculation Scheme of Synchronous Motor with Rectangular Conductors Considering Pulse Width Modulation Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient method for calculating AC copper loss in interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) with rectangular conductors, considering pulse width modulation (PWM) current harmonics. The inverter-fed current for driving IPMSM can be decomposed into fundamental and harmonic currents. The proposed method first utilizes magneto-static finite element analysis (MS FEA) to compute the magnetic vector potential (MVP) generated by the fundamental current. Next, the frozen permeability method linearizes the FEA model by keeping the permeability of iron core. A single harmonic current is input into linear-MS FEA to compute MVP without permanent magnet excitation. The MVP of other harmonic currents are derived using linear fitting. The linear fitting of MVP is validated with FEA. Finally, the AC copper loss is then calculated by summing the contributions from the MVP of each current component.

articleTitle: Homogenization Technique of Nanocrystalline Cores Considering the Inter-Laminar Eddy Currents
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Nanocrystalline core is widely used in high-frequency inductors for its standing performance of lower weights and losses. However, the electrical isolation among strips is ensured by the unevenness of the surface but not an absolute isolation by isolating layers like silicon steel sheets. To accurately calculate the loss of the nanocrystalline core, the inter-laminar eddy currents should be considered. We propose a homogenization technique of the nanocrystalline core considering the inter-laminar eddy currents. Compared to the results of the fine-meshed model, the proposed method is validated.

articleTitle: Variable Frequency Transformer Design for New Energy Microgrids and Grid Interconnections
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The variable frequency transformer (VFT) is investigated in this research for a new type of grid interconnection solution. Taking advantage of the moment of inertia of the rotor, the ability of the power system on coping with the sudden fluctuation can be enhanced. Aiming at a feasible design in this application condition, the design requirement is firstly specified based on the application configuration, and operation principle and kinetic energy analysis of the VFT. The distribution relationship between electromagnetic power and mechanical power, as well as the effects of torque change and grid-side frequency change on power transmission are analyzed to provide reference for the stable transmission and reliable control of VFT power. Then to meet the design specification, the design process is summarized. The design result is verified in a 15-kW design example and test platform.

articleTitle: Structural Aspects of Electromagneto-Quasistatic Field Formulations of Darwin-Type Derived in the Port-Hamiltonian System Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Electromagneto-quasistatic (EMQS) field formulations allow to model resistive, capacitive, and inductive field effects while neglecting wave propagation. These field formulations are based on the Darwin-Ampére equation and yield different approximations of the full set of Maxwell's equations depending on the choice of additional equations. Various discrete EMQS formulations are analyzed using the port-Hamiltonian system framework. It is shown that only combinations of the Darwin-Ampere equation and the Maxwell continuity equation yield port-Hamiltonian differential-algebraic system of equations (pH-DAE) which implies their numerical stability, energy conservation related to a specific EMQS variant of the Hamiltonian and dissipativity results.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction Model for Lithium-ion Batteries Using Transfer Learning Base on Long Short Term Memories
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper suggest Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) to analyze battery aging trend data and presents an algorithm designed for predicting the remaining life of lithium-ion batteries via transfer learning. The proposed algorithm utilizes a pre-trained battery model with LSTM-based transfer learning to forecast the remaining life based on cycles. To verify algorithm the predictions regarding the remaining battery life are conducted using data from NASA.

articleTitle: Computer Simulation of Magnetic Properties of Fe-Ni System Bilayer Ribbons Under Bending Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: We recently proposed Fe-Ni bilayer thin ribbons with uniaxial anisotropy using the inverse magnetoelastic effect for high-frequency driving devices. In the present study, to improve the soft magnetic properties of the ribbons, we developed a simulation method for two magnetic phases under mechanical stress. The slope of the hysteresis loop of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{F}{{\mathrm{e}}_{56}}\mathrm{N}{{\mathrm{i}}_{44}}{{F}}{{\mathrm{e}}_6}\mathrm{N}{{\mathrm{i}}_{94}}$</tex> model with stress was lower than that for no stress. This result implies that the stress induces a magnetic anisotropy, forming the hard axis in the excitation direction. As the variation of the loop by the stress was qualitatively consistent with the experimental results, we used the developed method to improve the soft magnetic properties. The simulation results suggested that reducing Fe content in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{F}{{\mathrm{e}}_{56}}\mathrm{N}{{\mathrm{i}}_{44}}$</tex> phase decreases the coercivity. Therefore, we prepared <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{F}{{\mathrm{e}}_{{100} - x}}\mathrm{N}{{\mathrm{i}}_x}{{F}}{{\mathrm{e}}_6}\mathrm{N}{{\mathrm{i}}_{94}}$</tex> ribbons and evaluated the coercivity. As a result, there was a significant difference in coercivity around <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x = 20$</tex> between the experiment and simulation. Further simulation found that a factor for this difference is attributed to the deviation from the ideal layer thickness ratio of 1:1.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Single Phase Flux Switching Reluctance Machine for Low Cost Turbo Machinery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Single Phase Flux Switching Reluctance Machines (SPFSRMs) are characterized by rugged structure, low cost and high reliability for high speed operation despite its poor starting capability. An analytical approach of performance evaluation for a 8/4 pole SPFSRM is developed in this paper. Firstly, using a lumped magnetic circuit model, the static performance is obtained. Then, a high precision saturated inductance model is constructed which can take the specific saturation effects and substantial influence of field current into consideration. At last, the motor transient performance can be precisely predicted in terms of winding current, torque and speed. A 2kW 8/4 pole prototype SPFSRM is designed together with the experimental correlation.

articleTitle: Propagation Characteristics of End-Winding Insulation Fatigue Damage in Variable Frequency Motor Under Multi-Field Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, the fatigue propagation mechanism of motor stator insulation damage under variable frequency drive is studied by combining theoretical analysis and finite element numerical simulation. Based on the magneto-thermo-solid coupling and fatigue damage theory, the stress-strain state, crack damage degree and propagation rate of motor stator insulation are analyzed. The crack damage propagation at different positions of the end winding outlet, middle and nose end is simulated and calculated by three-dimensional finite element method. It is found that the stress, strain and stress intensity factor of the end winding insulation at the outlet position change violently, which reflects that the crack damage is easier to expand and the propagation rate is greater. The results of this paper can provide reference for the evolution law, fault diagnosis and optimization design of insulation damage of variable frequency drive motor under complex working conditions.

articleTitle: Application of the Deep Operator Network (DeepONet) to Electromagnetic Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The physics-informed deep operator network (Deep-ONet) is a versatile and powerful machine learning algorithm to solve parametric ordinary/partial differential equations. Its ability to learn from functions gives much more flexibility in modeling physical phenomena with variable inputs. In this paper, the feasibility and effectiveness of applying the method for solving electromagnetic problems is studied. A numerical example is presented to demonstrate applicability of the method. A very good agreement between the physics-informed DeepONet results and the reference ones is observed. It is expected that this work will promote further applications of the neural networks in the design and analysis of electromagnetic devices.

articleTitle: Analysis of Split-Tooth Dual Winding Dual Magnet Machines with Low Mutual Inductance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a split-tooth dual winding dual magnet machine (SDWDM) with low mutual inductance is proposed and analyzed. Compared with conventional dual winding dual magnet machines (CDWDM), SDWDM has the obvious feature that the stator and rotor employ split-tooth structure and the winding employs fractional slot concentrated winding. The topology, electromagnetic performance, inductance characteristic, and efficiency are analyzed by finite element (FE) in turn. The results show that the mutual inductance of the proposed SDWDM is reduced by 53% compared to CDWDM. Moreover, copper loss is reduced and the efficiency is improved.

articleTitle: On the Equivalence of Working Volumes in Undermoded Reverberation Chambers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The equivalence of multiple working volumes (WV) are investigated in this work by the regime of state-of-the-art sensitivity analyis (SA) techniques. To this end, surrogate modeling was utilized to efficiently calculate the Sobol’ indices as a measure of uncertainty quantification (UQ). This approach helps to appraise the contributions of different configuration parameters in the lower frequency range, where the well-stirred condition cannot be established, yielding a proficient apparatus to ease the measurement process of parallelized radiated immunity (RIA) tests.

articleTitle: A Drive-Charging Integrated System Based on a New AC Flux-Regulation Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a drive-charging integrated system based on a new AC flux-regulation permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is proposed to be implemented for electric vehicles (EV s). In the driving mode, the hybrid energy system consisting of battery and supercapacitor is used to control AC flux-regulation PMSM through two sets of inverters, which can improve the speed regulation range and acceleration performance. In the charging mode, the inverter components and motor windings are multiplexed and formed into a two-stage charging topology to achieve electrical isolation and obtain high power and unit power factor charging capability. The control strategies in driving and charging modes are analyzed. The research results show that the proposed drive-charging integrated system can improve the system efficiency and reduce the volume and weight of EVs.

articleTitle: A Novel Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine with Axial Sandwich Structure for Flux Regulating Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel hybrid excited permanent magnet synchronous machine (HEPMSM) is presented which can enhance the capability of flux regulation and improve the flux leakage at the ends of rotor. The presented machine consists of two radial stators, two radial rotors and an axial stator, and has both radial and axial magnetic circuits. The side of the rotor is machined to form several sector rings so that the flux flows into both radial and axial stators. The machine has two magnetic pole structures, NN type and NS type, which will affect the flux path of the machine. The analysis shows that the machine has fine flux regulation capability and high power density, therefore, it has advantages in the fields of wide speed range such as electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Characteristic Analysis and Designing of 3kW E-Booster and Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: As the number of motors used in vehicles increases, the battery voltage of the vehicle is also being proposed from the conventional 12V to 48V. Most of the electric superchargers that boost the engine efficiency of the vehicle use 12V and rotate at ultra-high-speed. However, when 12V is used, there is a problem of loss due to high current and ultra-high-speed. Therefore, in this paper, we compared the characteristics by designing a conventional 12V ultra high speed electric supercharger and geared 48V high speed electric supercharger. We also analyzed the controller as well as the motor, and showed that the proposed model is superior in terms of integrated size and efficiency.

articleTitle: Development of Magnetic Eddy Current Testing for Opposite-Side Defect Detection in Ferromagnetic Steel Pipeline Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Conventional Magnetic Flux Leakage Testing (MFL) and Eddy Current Testing (ECT) have the limitation that they cannot detect and distinguish both side defects in ferromagnetic pipe inspection. To overcome this limitation, Magnetic Eddy Current Testing (MEC) has developed. it can detect both side defects and distinguish between surface and opposite side defects. In this paper, MEC system was introduced, and field and coil impedance perturbation due to opposite defects and surface defects were analyzed for distinguishing two defects. The principle of distinguishing two defects was explained through the transformer circuit. Simulation and experiment were conducted, and results showed that MEC can distinguish far-side and near-side defect through measurement of phase variation in signal.

articleTitle: Design of Anode Saturable Reactor Core Based on Electromagnetic-Thermal Simulation and Neural Network Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The separated structure of the anode saturable reactor (ASR) iron core makes it possible to change the arrangement of the iron core to affect heat exchange and reduce the risk of local thermal aging of insulation materials. Based on the electromagnetic thermal simulation results of the ASR, this study aims to improve the design of iron core thickness by using a neural network model with the same average temperature of 9 pairs of iron cores.

articleTitle: Investigation of Convergence of Linear Solvers in Electromagnetic Finite Element Analysis with Electric Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A fast linear solver for electromagnetic finite element analysis with electric circuit using a deflation technique with Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) is discussed. The authors have presented a deflated Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient (PCG) method that can reduce the cost of finite element analysis. The deflation technique decomposes the solution into fast and slowly converging components. The slow components can be solved by direct methods with low computational cost due to small dimensions. Therefore, the deflated PCC method can improve the convergence of PCG. However, the deflated PCG requires to find the slow components. In this study, a POD method with snapshots is introduced. Orthogonal vectors for the deflation are constructed from the snapshots. In contrast with well-known model order reduction with POD, the present method has same accuracy of solution as the PCG method. The authors have shown the present method in magnetostatic problem. In this study, the present method is applied to the electromagnetic finite element analysis with electric circuit. Moreover, the performance of the present method is compared with a subspace correction method. The numerical results show that the present method has good convergence in comparison with the conventional PCG method.

articleTitle: Calculation Method of d-Axis Inductance Considering Magnetic Saturation and Cross Coupling Effects Under Load Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In determining the characteristics of motors with salient polarity, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>- and q-axis inductances are important. These parameters are also critical for accurate equivalent circuit analysis. Conventional inductance calculation methods, which typically use constant no load flux linkage values induced by permanent magnets, often result in discontinuities in the d-axis inductance at current phase angles near 90 degrees, compromising the analysis precision. This paper introduces a novel, continuous d-axis inductance calculation method that accounts for magnetic saturation and cross coupling effects, enhancing the accuracy of such analyses. Furthermore, it includes a comparative study of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>- and q-axis inductance values and the magnetic flux of permanent magnets.

articleTitle: A Design Method of Reducing No-Load Harmonic Voltage of Interior Permanent Magnet Shaft Generator for Ships
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a design method for reducing the total harmonic distortion (THD) of the no-load voltage of the MW class interior permanent magnet (IPM) generator installed on the engine shaft of a ship propeller. The International Maritime Organization (IMO) is enforcing regulations on ships' greenhouse gas emissions, and the regulation has taken effect. In order to meet the regulation, many methods are being discussed, and permanent magnet shaft generators are one of the most effective alternatives. Therefore, the shaft generator is being researched and developed in many ways. This paper explains the method and the effect of the slot harmonic reduction for a large-capacity IPM shaft generator with an integer number of slots per pole (m). In the case of the IPM shaft generator with the integer number (m), the large slot harmonic could occur, which greatly distorts the no-load voltage. One simple method to reduce the slot harmonics of the no-load voltage is to increase the air gap, but as the air gap increases, the use of magnets increases to generate the same no-load voltage. It is not economical. In order to solve this issue, applying grooves to the surface of the rotor was introduced. We found that it can function as a filter that greatly reduces the slot harmonics (2m ± 1) of the no-load voltage without almost reducing the fundamental wave voltage. We will explain the groove effect with FEM simulations and the mathematical approach.

articleTitle: A Study on the Torque Characteristics of Permanent Magnet-Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor with Magnetic Neutral Point Movement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper is a study on the torque characteristics of a permanent magnet-assisted synchronous reluctance motor (PMa-SynRM) according to the arrangement of permanent magnets(PMs). In order to identify the movement of the magnetic neutral point due to the arrangement of PMs, a model with PMs inserted in the direction of rotation and a model with PMs inserted in the opposite direction of rotation were selected and compared by FEA. In addition, the causes of the movement of the maximum point of magnetic torque and the maximum point of reluctance torque and their influence on torque characteristics were examined. Finally, an excellent model is selected by comparing torque characteristics according to speed.

Author Keywords: Permanent magnet assistant Synchronous Reluctance Motor

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field Analysis Using Physics Informed Neural Network Considering Eddy Current
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The exploration of PINN (Physics Informed Neural Network) in research is still in its nascent stages globally, with a notable dearth of studies focusing on electromagnetic field analysis. In response to this gap, this paper introduces a novel approach for eddy current analysis employing a transfer learning-based discrete differentiation method within the framework of a PINN. While discrete differentiation methods offer the advantage of low model complexity and rapid analysis, they encounter challenges in eddy current analysis due to the need for learning at each time step. This paper addresses these challenges through the application of transfer learning techniques. Our findings demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces the total analysis time in time-dependent scenarios compared to traditional Finite Element Method (FEM) approaches.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Field Interactions on Silver Nanospheres and Silver Nanowires
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this work, silver nanospheres and silver nanowires (AgNWs), which are essential in most applications in biosensing, surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS), and nanoplasmonics, are modeled in computer environment. The modeling includes the assessment of the nanoparticle's absorptions and extinctions. In the simulation results, the red-shift that should be observed with the increase in sphere diameter can be clearly seen. In addition, the characteristic peaks that should be seen for AgNW are also observed.

articleTitle: Investigation of Winding Power Loss in Flux Modulated Permanent Magnet Machine Considering Multi-Physics Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In order to accurately analyze the winding power loss in field modulation permanent magnet machine, the power loss model comprehensively considering the influence of the skin effect, the proximity effect, the thermal effect, and different winding topologies on winding eddy current loss is established in this paper. The characteristics of the winding resistance is analyzed, where the harmonic, conductor size, and number of parallel strands are taken into account. The calculated winding power loss based on the proposed analytical model is compared with the simulation results obtained by traditional finite element analysis. Then, the experiment for measuring winding resistance and AC power loss under different current excitations is carried out. Compared to the finite-element modeling approach that is often used for AC winding copper loss, the key advantages of the proposed model are high accuracy and low time consumption.

articleTitle: Anisotropic Vector Hysteresis Modeling Under Multiaxial Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A model for predicting the vector hysteresis properties of non-oriented steel sheets under multiaxial stress is proposed. In this model, the sensibility of mechanical stress is accounted for both in the reversible and irreversible magnetization based on the magneto-elastic energy of single crystal and domain motion theory. Comparisons between measured and calculated curves and losses are performed to validate the model.

articleTitle: Structural Design and Electromagnetic Performance Analysis of 50Mvar HTS Synchronous Condenser
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In the paper, the overall structure and electromagnetic design parameters of a new high temperature superconducting (HTS) synchronous condenser with a capacity of 50Mvar is preliminary presented. Stator and rotor as well cooling method of the HTS condenser is introduced in detail, and a two-dimensional simulation model is established by finite element method (FEM) for analyzing electromagnetic characteristics. As the result, the air gap flux density of the HTS synchronous condenser is closely to 1.6T, and the electromotive force (EMF) increases linearly with exciting current.

articleTitle: Efficient Shape Uncertainty Quantification for the TESLA Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In our contribution, we present an efficient shape uncertainty quantification method based on closed-form shape derivatives for the Maxwell eigenvalue problem. We demonstrate our algorithm for the 9-cell TESLA cavity which is subject to misalignment due to imperfections in the manufacturing process and compare the performance of our approach to the classic Monte Carlo method. In this comparison, we observe a drastic increase in efficiency.

articleTitle: Parameter and Topology Optimization Method for IPM Motors using Multimodal Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This study proposes a novel parameter and topology optimization method for an interior permanent magnet synchronous motor using a multimodal neural network. The optimized shape obtained by the proposed method improves the manufacturability compared to the conventional method. In addition, the computational time of the optimization using the proposed method is reduced by about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$99.9{{\% }}$</tex> compared to the optimization using only the finite element method.

articleTitle: Detection and Location Estimate of External Surface Defects Using Velocity Effects from Double-Sided Quadrupole Permanent Magnets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The round bar steel of C45 steel material is widely used as a general machine part material, such as springs for automobiles. This round steel bar requires high-speed surface defect inspection during the manufacturing process. In this research, an inspection method is proposed in which a round steel bar is moved at a high speed of 1m/s in a ring-shaped permanent magnet to surface defect in the round steel bar. In addition, the possibility of estimating the location of defects is also shown by using double-sided quadrupole permanent magnets.

articleTitle: Study on Rotor Bar Loss Due to Space Harmonics of Line Start Synchronous Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The existing papers on Line Start Synchronous Reluctance Motor (LS-SynRM) were mainly about design methods to achieve high efficiency without considering rotor bar loss, but in reality, rotor bar loss is caused by harmonics. Therefore, this paper analyzed the effect of rotor bar copper loss caused by harmonics on LS-SynRM.

articleTitle: Characteristic Analysis of Two-Phase Stator-Permanent-Magnet Hybrid Stepping Machines with Radial and Tangential Magnetization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Hybrid stepping machines (HSMs) are preferred in applications where high precision, low-cost positioning and high torque, since they can be controlled with no feedback control and have many advantages of higher torque and efficiency over the other types of stepping machines. In this paper, a stator-permanent-magnet HSM (SPMHSM) with radial magnetization (RM) is proposed and compared with that with Tangential magnetization (TM). Firstly, the structure of proposed machine is introduced and its operation principle is analyzed by describing the variation in the armature magnet field versus current. Secondly, based on the similar electrical load and the amount of PM, the SPMHSM with RM is designed. Thirdly, the electromagnetic performance including back-electromotive force, magnetic density and output torque of the two machines are analyzed. The simulation results indicate the SPMHSM with RM can alleviate the magnetic saturation of stator core, and has a wilder current and torque range.

articleTitle: Study on Equivalent 2-D Finite Element Analysis Model for Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Motor Considering the End Effects in Radial Direction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: With recent developments in analysis and manufacturing technology, interest in axial flux permanent magnet motor (AFPMM) is increasing. To accurately analyze AFPMM, 3-dimensional finite element analysis (3-D FEA) is required. However, although 3-D FEA provides high accuracy, it requires significant analysis time and resources. In this paper, we propose a equivalent 2-dimensional finite element analysis (2-D FEA) model to overcome the shortcomings of 3-D FEA. To improve the analysis accuracy of the 2-D equivalent model, we propose an equivalent 2-D FEA model of an AFPMM that considers the radial end effect. After dividing the 3-D model in the radial direction to build a 2-D equivalent model, the accuracy of analysis is improved by using a model that can take into account the leakage flux occurring in the radial direction for the radial innermost and outermost equivalent models. The analysis precision using the equivalent 2-D FEA model will be verified by comparing it with the analysis results of the 3-D FEA.

articleTitle: Multiscale Hysteresis Model of Electrical Steel Sheet in Finite Element Simulation of Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this abstract, the multiscale model incorporates an energy based hysteresis model for ferromagnetic material. The coherent rotational phenomena are considered by letting the magnetic domains rotates with the applied field. Finally, the model of steel sheets is simulated in a finite element model of a transformer.

articleTitle: Analytical Study and Experimental Verification of Electromagnetic Vibration Sources and Optimization of Rotor Skew in Surface Mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a method for calculating the cogging torque and air-gap flux density of a surface mounted permanent magnet machine was studied. First, a simplified model of the machine to be analyzed was presented, and the magnetic vector potential was defined using a governing equation after dividing the region by section. The air gap flux density was derived using appropriate boundary conditions, and based on this, the cogging torque was calculated. The results of the simplified analytical model were validated using the finite element method (FEM) and experiments, and the proposed method was used to investigate the influence of rotor skew on cogging torque.

articleTitle: Study on Transformer Electric Field in Different Degrees of Insulation Aging Considering Temperature Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper investigates the thermal aging of transformer insulation systems through a comprehensive approach involving aging experiments and simulation analyses. Primarily, the study explores the experimental and simulated aspects of transformer temperature elevation, providing detailed insights into the temperature rise phenomenon. To achieve predetermined temperature thresholds, the transformer is equipped with an insulation and temperature control system. Subsequently, the investigation delves into the aging of transformer oil under specific temperature conditions, presenting aging results for transformer oil subjected to 5 cycles. Finally, leveraging finite element software, the electric field distribution of the transformer is meticulously calculated, elucidating characteristics of electric field distribution in transformer oil under varying aging conditions. Building upon the experimental results of transformer aging, the paper scrutinizes the insulation aging state and electric field distribution of transformers in active service. This research provides a foundational framework for evaluating transformer service life and formulating preventative measures against insulation failure.

articleTitle: Modeling of Magnetic Properties of Silicon Steel Sheets under DC Bias based on Multi-Scale Dynamic Jiles–Atherton Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In order to model the hysteresis characteristics of electrical steel sheets under dc bias from the perspective of the physical magnetization mechanism, a dynamic Jiles–Atherton (J-A) hysteresis model combined with a simplified multi-scale model is used, and based on the statistical theory of losses, the J-A hysteresis model is dynamically realized by considering eddy current loss and excess loss. The dc magnetic flux density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf> and magnetic field strength <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf> are introduced to solve the deviation of the hysteresis loop under the action of dc bias. And defining <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> in the excess loss as a function of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf> in order to estimate the excess loss. Comparative analysis was conducted using experimental data. The analytical results verified the effectiveness of the model in representing the hysteresis characteristics under dc bias.

articleTitle: A Posteriori Error Estimators for Quantity of Interest in Eddy Current-Based Non-Destructive Testings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The accuracy of finite element simulations for eddy current-based non-destructive testing is impeded by numerical errors associated with the mesh. This study introduces a goal-oriented error estimate for eddy current problems, specifically focusing on the quantity of interest. A more practical interpretation is provided, and numerical examples illustrate the potential applications of the proposed estimator.

articleTitle: Optimum Parameter Selection for Accurate FDTD Simulations in Dispersive Media
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Modifying the constitutive parameters of the background media is a technique that enables the mitigation of numerical dispersion errors in finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations, when wave propagation in non-dispersive materials is modeled. For cases where material dispersion is present, we propose a methodology that alters the parameters of the typical Lorentz model, so that the impact of numerical errors is controlled in two-dimensional FDTD studies.

articleTitle: Hybrid Boundary Element – Physics Informed Neural Network Formulation for Electromagnetics Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this contribution the authors propose a hybrid BEM-PINN method for the resolution of the partial differential equations arising in electromagnetism. The method retains the advantages of both integral methods (compact representation and no need to mesh large domains) as well as differential methods, where the term “differential” is here referred to the Automatic Differentiation implemented during the PINN training. The method is easy to implement and adds an additional flexibility to PINN applications.

articleTitle: Alternative PM Motor Configurations Comparison for UAV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The interest of industry domain and research community for the performance estimation of 3D-printed electrical machines grows rapidly, focusing on challenges that are related to the design and construction of high-speed motors with high efficiency and power density. Since there are plenty high-frequency applications, such as the unmanned aerial vehicles, that impose high-performance requirements and strict mass constraints, the additive manufacturing technique could provide customizable, scalable and cost-efficient motor design solutions. By avoiding off-the-shelf solutions, the suitability of a particular 3D-printed magnetic iron material (which is commercially available) is investigated here for the design and manufacturing of the stator core of a low-power and high-speed permanent magnet synchronous motor. The motor could be used to drive the UAV's auxiliary systems. A prototype is constructed and the motor's electromagnetic behavior is estimated through finite element analysis and experiments. The obtained results validate both the machine's performance and the effectiveness of the proposed material's modeling procedure.

articleTitle: A Novel Mesh-Based Reluctance Network Model for Magnetic Lead Screw
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a mesh-based reluctance network (MBRN) model is proposed for Magnetic Lead Screws (MLS). The MBRN model divides the internal magnetic field of the MLS into several uniform mesh elements. The proposed model can be used to predict the performance of the MLS, including the air-gap flux density and thrust force. In order to verify the reliability of the MBRN model, its accuracy is verified by comparing it with the finite element analysis.

articleTitle: Shape Sensitivity Analysis for Optimal Design of Time-Harmonic Electroquasistatic System based on Continuum Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a continuum-based sensitivity analysis for an optimal shape design of a time-harmonic electroquasistatic (EQS) system. The material derivative concept, which originates from continuum mechanics, is employed for deriving the shape sensitivity formula. All the boundaries of the EQS system are considered its design variables. The Lagrange multiplier method, adjoint variable technique, and variational identity are sequentially applied to the material derivative of an augmented objective function. Thereby, the sensitivity formula is obtained in an analytical form and expressed by a boundary integral. Since the continuum shape sensitivity is evaluated prior to the discretization process of the finite element method (FEM), it can be easily and accurately calculated using commerical FEM software. The smooth expression of the shape-variation is implemented by combining the shape sensitivity with the level-set method. The shape optimization problem in the three-dimension is presented to demonstrate the theoretical validity and numerical feasibility of this study.

articleTitle: An Optimization Method for Coil Design Problems Based on Physarum Polycephalum Algorithm and Evolutionary Computation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a new optimization approach for coil design problems. To obtain a connected path, the coil design task is formulated as an optimum routing problem. In order to solve the routing problem, the physarum polycephalum algorithm is employed and it is combined with evolutionary computations. It is shown that the proposed method can find a coil design for the generation of target uniform magnetic distribution.

articleTitle: DC-link Voltage Control Strategy Considering Vessel Condition for Efficiency Improvement of IH Cooktops with PFC Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a variable DC-link voltage (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm{V}_{\text{DC}}}$</tex> control method (VDCVM) considering the size of the vessel condition of the induction heating (IH) cooktops with a Power Factor Correction (PFC) rectifier. If the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm{V}_{\text{DC}}}$</tex> is controlled at a constant value, the switching frequency should be operated far from the designed resonant network according to the smaller vessel condition. Therefore, in this paper, VDCVM is applied to increase the heating performance for each vessel by enhancing system efficiency. The validity of the proposed control method is verified through loss and efficiency analysis with simulation.

articleTitle: Estimation of Local Demagnetization in Ferrite Magnet Using Pinching-Type Sigmoid Function Based on Gradient Method (P-SiGrad)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In recent years, the development of electric vehicles (EVs) is being actively pursued. Several permanent magnet synchronous motors are installed in EVs. Revealing the magnetization state inside PMs is essential at the early design stage to improve the manufacturing quality of permanent magnet (PM) motors. Therefore, a method known as SiGrad has been developed by the authors to numerically estimate the magnetization distribution using the magnetic flux density measured around PMs. Consequently, the effective performance of SiGrad in the PM estimation with the homogeneous magnetization distribution is demonstrated. However, the performance of the estimation of the PM with inhomogeneous distribution in the demagnetized region is not investigated. In this study, the applicability of SiGrad to demagnetized magnetization estimation is verified, and the pinching-type SiGrad (P-Sigrad) is newly proposed to improve the estimation accuracy of SiGrad.

articleTitle: A Second-Order Split-Step Precise Integration Time Domain Method for Solving Maxwell's Equations and its Numerical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Based on the three-stage split-step scheme, a second-order split-step precise-integration time-domain (SS2-PITD) method is proposed for solving Maxwell's equations, which has a better performance in computational accuracy and efficiency than the previously proposed split-step precise-integration time-domain (SS1-PITD) method. Then, the numerical stability of the SS2- PITD method is analyzed, showing that the time step size in SS2-PITD can be a value much larger than the Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy limit. Finally, numerical examples are simulated to show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Multi-objective Optimization Algorithm and its Application to Designs of Eletromagnetic Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel hybrid multi-objective optimization (MOO) algorithm is proposed by combining the improved Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA) with the improved NSGA-II. The original SSA is improved by introduction of the population updating mechanism of Moth-flame Optimization (MFO) algorithm and by adopting adaptive mutation probability; meanwhile, the NSGA-II is enhanced by using Latin hypervolume sampling and dynamical selection mechanism of crossover and mutation operators. Numerical results of cases including TEAM22 benchmark problem and topology optimization problem of an electromagnetic actuator prototype demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed hybrid algorithm.

articleTitle: Analysis and Reduction of Detent Force in Flat Permanent Magnet Linear Motor with Inner-Arc Auxiliary Teeth
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents an improved flat permanent magnet linear motor (FPMLM) structure with inner-arc auxiliary teeth to reduce detent force. The parameters that affect detent force are determined by using Fourier analysis method. The influences of slot opening, the side slot widths and the size of end teeth on detent force are investigated, the optimal dimension parameters are obtained by Differential Evolution (DE) algorithm. For verifying the advantages of the improved structure, two FPMLMs with traditional and improved structures are analyzed using finite-element method (FEM), the analytical analysis is verified by extensive 3-D numerical computations. The results show that the proposed structure can significantly reduce the detent force with the least sacrifice of electromagnetic performance.

articleTitle: Novel Salient Stator Pole-Shoe Structure for Reducing the Shaft Voltage of the PMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) are exposed to harmful bearing currents and shaft voltage which affect their lifetime. This study suggests a novel salient stator pole-shoe structure (SSPS) to suppress the shaft voltage and bearing current. The SSPS interferes with the effect of the electric field between the coil and the rotor, thereby reducing winding-to-rotor capacitance C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">wer</inf>, which is a major factor for the shaft voltage. The electrostatic finite element analysis (FEA) is performed to calculate the parasitic capacitance and compare the difference between the SSPS and the classical pole shoe model. To validate the effectiveness of the SSPS, the magnetic field transient FEA is performed comparing with classical model. Finally, the shaft voltage of two prototypes (SSPS and classical model) is verified by experiment.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of High Torque Density Robotic Joint Motors Based on Equivalent Magnetic Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The electric drive method is considered to be one of the most promising methods for robots, and the joint motors play a crucial role in the performance of robots. In order to improve the torque density of the joint motor, this paper does not use a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM), but uses the magnetic field modulation effect to design a permanent magnet vernier motor (PMVM). In this paper, the performance index of the joint motor is firstly determined according to the robot requirements, and several slot-pole fits that meet the requirements are given. Then, the equivalent magnetic circuit (EMC) model of the joint motor was established, and the electromagnetic performance of the joint motor was theoretically deduced and compared with the finite element analysis. The prototype was fabricated and experimentally tested.

articleTitle: Design of Anti-Saturated Coil for Robust Wireless Power Transfer in Magnetic Latching System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The paper proposed an anti-saturated coil to alleviate magnetic saturation and inductance reduction in wireless power transfer systems with permanent magnets. The proposed anti-saturated coil forms a magnetic field in the opposite direction of the permanent magnet, canceling out the influence of the permanent magnet. Therefore, the magnetic material of the WPT system allows operation in the linear region. The effectiveness of the anti-saturated coil was proven through simulation, and it was demonstrated that applying the proposed coil improved the inductance reduction rate by about 10% compared to the system without it.

articleTitle: Magnetic Circuit Analysis of Hybrid Excitation Flux Switching Motor with Non-uniform Auxiliary Air Gap
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this article, a new non-uniformed auxiliary air gap is proposed to improve the output torque of the hybrid excitation flux switching motors (HEFSMs). A magnetic circuit model (MCM) is developed to predict the flux regulation capability of the HEFSM and the results are calculated and compared to finite-element analysis (FEA) results so that the validity of the MCM is verified.

articleTitle: Model Order Reduction of Transient Magnetic Field Based on POD and DEIM Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) has been widely applied to reduce the numerical computation time and memory storage requirements of the finite element. When the nonlinear problems of ferromagnetic materials are dealt in time domain, the high computational costs are needed due to the interactive process. This paper proposes to combine POD method with discrete empirical interpolation method (DEIM) to effectively deal with nonlinear transient magnetic field problems of transformer, and the calculated results are compared with the tested ones.

articleTitle: Parametrized Cauer Ladder Network Equations for Reduced Representation of Nonlinear Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Parametrized Cauer ladder network equations are derived for the reduced representation of the nonlinear eddy-current field. The variation of basis functions of the magnetic field is included in the network equation for accurate tracing of the parameter transition with respect to magnetic saturation degree. Several reasonable formulations using reluctivity and differential reluctivity are proposed without calculating the parameter variation terms directly.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization of Rotor Core Structure to Reduce Permanent Magnet Eddy Current Losses in Interior Permanent-Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Recently, interior permanent magnet synchronous motors (IPMSMs) are widely used in various industrial machines owing to their high torque efficiency, and so on. However, when driving IPMSMs at high speeds, the efficiency of IPMSMs is deteriorated, and demagnetization of the permanent magnets (PMs) are caused by the eddy current losses generated in the PMs. To reduce the eddy current losses in PMs, topology optimization (TO) is an effective method in terms of design freedom and the ability to radically change the structure. TO using sensitivity analysis is effective for problems that require long computation time, such as nonlinear time-domain analysis. Therefore, in this paper, TDAVM-based and TO is applied to the rotor of IPMSM to reduce the eddy current loss. As a result, the effective magnetic structure of IPMSM is derived.

articleTitle: Simulation-Driven Machine Learning for Solving the Inverse Problem of PCB-Based Tilt-Inductive Position Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: PCB-based Inductive Position Sensors (IPS) are advantageous with respect to resistive, capacitive or Hall-effect alternatives since they allow for contactless sensors that are immune to stray fields and robust to temperature changes, all while being easy to manifacture by using conventional PCB fabrication techniques. In this work we present an IPS design for measuring the angle of a target conductor with respect to the sensing coils, and the distance between them. Simulations are used to build a dataset for training a neural network to solve the inverse problem of estimating tilt and airgap from the measured voltages. The trained network is tested against experimental data measured from a physical prototype.

articleTitle: Topological Design of a Novel Magnetically Saturated Bridge Arm Reactor with Controllable Inductance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Circulating currents and fault currents in MMC systems can pose a threat to the stable operation of the system. In this paper, a novel magnetically saturated bridge arm reactor topology is proposed, its operating principle is analyzed, and the simulation verification of electromagnetic characteristics is carried out. It has the characteristic of variable inductance and suppresses the above currents without affecting the normal operation of the system.

articleTitle: A Fast Multiscale Numerical Algorithm for Coupling Dynamics of the Bubble in Insulating Oil Under the Electric Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The presence of bubbles in the transformer oil is very prone to cause partial discharges in the oil, which affects the insulation characteristics. Therefore, it is of vital importance to study the severity of the electric field distortion and the dynamic characteristics of the bubble under this physical model of gas-liquid two-phase flow. In this paper, a multiscale finite element method of electric field coupled with the dynamic characteristics of the bubble is proposed. The coupling between the electrostatic field and the hydrodynamic field is established through the level set function. The level set function is an output of data from the hydrodynamic field for the position of the bubble and at the same time an input of data for the description of the interpolation function when solving for the electric field by the extended finite element method. Unlike the conventional finite element method, this algorithm eliminates the need to re-dissect the elements at each time step, and thus can greatly reduce the solution time while maintaining accuracy.

articleTitle: S-domain FE Analysis of Magneto-quasi-static Problem Using Discrete Laplace Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The frequency domain finite element (FE) method is utilized to study the magneto problem with the large time constant, as it allows for the avoidance of tedious computation to meet steady state in the time domain. However, frequency domain FEM has its limitations; for instance, it cannot consider the initial value in simulations. This paper proposes a s-domain FE method which solves steady-state magnetic field based on initial state. The method can convert the time-dependent excitation onto s-domain using discrete Laplace transform and solve the governing equations in the s-domain. To verify the correctness of this method, a 35kV transformer model is taken as a numerical example to study the magnetic field.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Parameter Design and Finite Element Analysis of a Novel Dual-Stator Electric-Thermal Output Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The development of wind power has received increasing attention. However, with the large-scale grid connection of wind power, there is great uncertainty in the power grid.
