To this end, a novel electric-thermal output machine is needed to simultaneously convert wind energy into electrical and thermal energy. The generated thermal energy can be directly supplied to users or used to drive a turbine generator set, thereby transforming wind power generation from uncontrollable to controllable and meeting the requirements for safe and reliable operation of the power grid. In this paper, a method for designing the electromagnetic parameters of a dual-stator electric-thermal output machine is proposed. According to the design idea from outside to inside, the outer stator, rotor and inner stator are designed, and then the loaded characteristics of the designed motor are analyzed based on finite element simulation.

articleTitle: Magnetic Force Calculation Using Virtual Air Gap Penetrating Finite Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In the finite element method (FEM), a whole space is formed using meshes, and these meshes are organized based on material boundaries to define domains for magnetic force calculations. However, with the help of the virtual air-gap concept, it is also possible to obtain a magnetic force in a domain drawn independently regardless of the boundaries of objects in an environment in which elements and physical quantities are already determined. Then, repetitive work can be performed by configuring the magnetic force calculation area in post-processing without meshes shape correction and recalculation. This also serves to delineate the characteristics of computational tools for the precise representation of magnetic forces within the material.

articleTitle: A Study on the Characteristics of Electromagnetic Field of Twin-Inverter System Traction Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To generate high torque, EV towing motors require a large current. To address the burden of the system due to high current, a Twin-Inverter System with different inverter connections for each parallel circuit is applied. In this paper, we study the electromagnetic properties that occur when one of the inverters of the traction IPMSM driven by the Twin-Inverter System is not operating normally due to failure.

articleTitle: Investigation of Dual-Side Consequent-Pole Permanent Magnet Machine with Improved Magnetic Field Modulation Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In order to further improve the torque density and power factor of permanent magnet (PM) machines with magnetic gear effect, a dual-side consequent-pole PM machine (DCPMM) is proposed in this paper. Both stator and rotor are incorporated with a consequent-pole PM arrangement. The ferromagnetic poles of the rotor and stator are utilized to modulate the magnetic field excited by stator-PM and rotor-PM, namely, the bidirectional modulation effect. The topology, operation principle, and design considerations of the proposed DCPMM are analyzed. Then, the electromagnetic performances of the proposed machine with different excitation methods are evaluated and compared by finite-element analysis. The employment of dual-side PM excitation is beneficial to enhance air-gap flux densities and torque production capability. The results demonstrate that the proposed machine can produce superior torque production with low torque ripple, great overload capability, and a high power factor.

articleTitle: State Space Modelling of Microstrip Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Microstrip transmission lines are a specific type of transmission lines in the high frequency (HF) regime. Such microstrips are commonly used for test fixtures in HF-measurements, e.g. for broadband characterization of HF - devices. For accurate measurement of the device under test (DUT), a priori knowledge of the frequency behaviour of the microstrip line is needed. In the present work, a broadband state space model for microstrip transmission lines is proposed. The equivalent circuit parameters of the microstrip are extracted by means of quasi-3D finite element simulations.

articleTitle: Design of a High Reliability and High Performance Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Used in Oil-Submersible Electric Pump System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Submersible permanent magnet synchronous motors (SPMSM) operate in harsh and complex environments, so reliability is the basis of motor design. However, the diameter limitations of the oil pipe and the limitation of slot fill factor make the performance of SPMSMs lower than the conventional PMSMs. This paper analyzed the design limitations in SPMSMs, pointing out the necessity of saturated magnetic circuit design, and gives a high-reliability and high-performance scheme based on the finite element method (FEM). The single-layer winding and parallel slots are adopted in stator to improve the empirical slot fill factor, and the double-layer “1+V” type permanent magnets (PMs) are adopted in rotor to improve the saliency ratio and torque. Furthermore, the maximum rotor stress, the anti-demagnetization performance of the PMs and the steady-state temperature rise of the motor were also calculated in this paper. Finally, the proposed SPMSM is fabricated and tested to confirm its feasibility.

articleTitle: Multidirectional Magnetic Field Decoupling Model Based on Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Active magnetic compensation is required to achieve near-zero magnetic environment for Magnetocardiography (MCG). The coupling relations between the magnetic fields of passive field cause difficulties in compensation. In this paper, we establish a multidirectional magnetic field decoupling model which build adjustive vector and unidirectional magnetic field matrix (AV-UMFM) equations. Based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm, the adjustive vector of the model can be acquired despite ill-conditioned problems. Finally, adjustive vector controls currents to simultaneously compensate for multidirectional residual magnetic fields and builds magnetic compensation system.

articleTitle: A Study on Reduction of AC Copper Loss According to Pole/Slot Combination of EV Traction Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper is about reducing AC copper loss of an EV traction motor with a maximum speed of 21000 rpm. Recently, as a high-power density design method for traction motors for EVs, the advantages of high slot fill factor and short end turns of hairpin windings have emerged. However, when using hairpin windings, AC copper loss increases at higher speeds, greatly reducing efficiency and power density, so measures to reduce this loss are necessary. AC copper loss is largely divided into skin effect, proximity effect, and eddy current loss due to leakage magnetic flux, which all increase in proportion to the frequency of use. In this paper, the characteristics according to pole/slot combination were analyzed by comparing the AC copper loss and output characteristics at the rated and maximum speed operating points of the 8p/48s model and the 6p/36s model.

articleTitle: Development of High-Speed Magnetization Estimator with Multi-Estimation Points in Permanent Magnet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) are commonly used in electric vehicles, and their torque characteristics depend on the magnetization distribution (MD) in permanent magnets (PMs). Therefore, the application of inaccurately magnetized PMs can cause unexpected vibrations and noise in PMSMs. In this study, a magnetization estimation system is developed using multiple Hall sensors to measure the magnetic flux density around the PM and estimate the MD in a quick and inexpensive manner.

articleTitle: Effective Interface Condition for Electromagnetic Shielding Using the T-Φ-Formulation in 3D
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Thin shell models replace electromagnetic shields with an interface in the finite element mesh, which leads to less degrees of freedom and better conditioned finite elements. However, they depend on approximations by analytical solutions or on expansions by suitable basis functions. This work presents an effective material approach which does not require any additional unknowns inside the shield, replacing the eddy current problem with an effective stationary field problem on the outside domain.

articleTitle: Accelerated 3D Analysis of Metasurfaces for RIS Applications by Characteristic Basis Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A fast 3D numerical solver based on an electric field integral equation (EFIE) formulation is developed for analyzing metasurfaces (MTSs) in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) applications. As part of the numerical model, a new methodology is introduced for the systematic generation of characteristic basis functions (CBFs). The CBFs provide a global approximation function set for the surface currents on PEC patches of the MTS cells with significantly fewer unknowns than regular localized expansion functions. Verification results are also provided.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Broadband Vibrational Energy Harvester Based on Switchable Dynamical System Using Electropermanent Magnet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a new broadband vibrational energy harvester (VEH) based on switchable dynamical systems using an electropermanent magnet (EPM). A broadband harvesting characteristic is evaluated by solving governing equations of the VEH numerically. The effectiveness of the proposed VEH is verified by comparing a drastic increase in a harvested power with a Joule loss due to a short-time pulsed current applied to the EPM.

articleTitle: Comparison of Characteristics According to Permanent Magnet Arrangement of Permanent Magnet Linear Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This study focuses on the comparative analysis of permanent magnet linear synchronous generators (PMLSG) with different magnetization arrangements. Using finite element analysis (FEA), this paper compares the performance analysis according to three magnetization arrangements of PMLSG with parallel, Halbach, and axial array PM. Comparison models are designed with identical rated output power, overall dimensions, air gap, and stator geometry to ensure reliability of comparison results. An experimental setup, including a rotary motor and a slider-crank mechanism, was developed to simulate wave motion and validate the FEA models. Comparative analysis between FEA results and experimental data demonstrated a high degree of correlation, affirming the validity of the analytical models.

articleTitle: Design of Shaft Voltage Reduction Shield Considering Eddy Current Loss of IPMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this study, shaft voltage was reduced by applying a flexible printed circuit board (FPCB)-based shield to an interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM). However, as the shield is applied, high heat is generated inside the motor and the shield. Therefore, a method of lowering the temperature inside the motor and the shield through the optimal design of the shield is proposed.

articleTitle: Utilizing an Efficient Magnetic Equivalent Circuit Model and Manifold Mapping Method for Two-Level Optimization of Axial Flux Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a two-level optimization algorithm is developed based on rapid magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC) model and manifold mapping (MM) method. The performance of an axial flux permanent magnet machine (AFPM) is optimized using this approach. The rapid MEC model based on grid division exhibits significant computational efficiency, while reducing the influence of artificial factors in modeling process. Further, quantitative comparison of the error performance under different combinations of divisions are carried out. Subsequently, coarse and fine models are selected, respectively. The iterative process indicates that the modeling approach enables the coarse model to correctly follow the trends of fine model as input changes. As a result, the fast convergence of the MM is successfully achieved.

articleTitle: Fast Estimation System of Permanent Magnet Magnetization Using 2D-Arrayed Hall Sensors Combined with Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Loading permanent magnets (PMs) is essential for realization of high-output of electromagnetic machines such as the permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs). In the most of the PMSMs, the torque performance is dependent on the magnetization distribution of the PM. Therefore, on the manufacturing process of PMSMs, a fast estimation instrumentation is substantially required. In this paper, to estimate the PM magnetization quickly and accurately, a special instrumentation comprising the 2D-arrayed Hall sensors and deep neural network is developed.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Finite Element Method Applied in 3D Nonlinear Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Numerical calculation of electromagnetic fields plays an important role in the design of electrical equipment. However, due to the special structure of certain equipment, traditional numerical calculation methods often meet great difficulties when dealing with such problems. For example, in the design process of the transformer core, it is difficult to calculate the electromagnetic field around the core due to the nonlinearity of the material, the huge size difference between the silicon steel sheet and the core, and the complexity of the air gap distribution. Taking the widely used commercial numerical calculation software as an example, the finite element method is used in the numerical calculation process, and many elements and nodes are used in the process. This will lead to a complex mesh and cost a lot of computing resources and a long computing time. This paper improves on the widely used conventional finite element method (CFEM) and proposes a multi-scale finite element method (MSFEM). Using a special interpolation built with an enrichment function, the elements are not restricted by media or geometry. Taking Team Workshop problem 10 as a numerical example, the accuracy of this method and the saving of computational costs have been proved.

articleTitle: The Harmonic-Balanced Finite Element Method Coupled with Dynamic Hysteresis Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Considering the magnetic hysteresis, the harmonic-balanced finite element method coupled with the dynamic hysteresis model is proposed. The loss separation theory and the Preisach model are applied for generating the hysteresis model. To improve the convergence characteristics, the secant method and the fixed-point technique are applied for nonlinear problems. The simulation results are validated by comparing to the experiment results of the silicon lamination core under the excitation of DC-bias.

articleTitle: Grounding Current Mechanism of Converter Transformer Core and Clamp
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper analyzes the mechanism of grounding current generation in the core and clamp of converter transformers, which is much higher than that of ordinary power transformers in recent years. Firstly, factors such as the connection type, grounding method, iron core type, voltage level, voltage harmonics, DC bias and age of the converter transformer are taken into consideration for mechanism analysis. Then, the model of the HVDC system was established and the grounding current of the converter transformer was analyzed and calculated. Finally, the on-site grounding current was compared with the calculated results to verify the correctness of the mechanism proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: An Efficient Hybrid DC Circuit Breaker Based on Current Commutation With Mechanical and Power Electronics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This study proposes an efficient hybrid DC Circuit breaker (DCCB) based on current commutation with mechanical and power electronics (MPE). An efficient MPE DCCB neglects the on-state losses by using a mechanical monostable switch instead of a solid-state switch located in the main current branch. When a short-circuit fault occurs, the mechanical monostable switch commutates the fault current from the main current branch to the commutation branch, which comprises a solid-state switch. Moreover, an efficient MPE DCCB can reduce the number of solid-state switches by dividing the transient interruption voltage (TIV) between a mechanical fast-switch and a solid-state switch. The DC interruption capability of the proposed MPE DCCB was confirmed through a DC interruption test.

articleTitle: Parametric Model Order Reduction of Darwin Model Considering Nonlinear Magnetic Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a new parametric model order reduction technique of the Darwin model for electromagnetic apparatuses with nonlinear magnetic materials. This method allows us to perform the time-domain analysis much faster than the finite element analysis.

articleTitle: Novel Hybrid 3-D Shape Optimization Method Combining Parameter and Topology Optimizations: Application to Permanent Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel hybrid 3-D shape optimization method combining the parameter and topology optimizations. In the proposed optimization, the 3-D magnetic core shape is determined by topology optimization, whereas the magnet shape is determined by parameter optimization using the Boolean operation. It is shown that the 3-D optimized rotor structure leads to superior torque performance than the reference model which has uniform rotor structure along the rotating shaft.

articleTitle: Analysis of an Inductive Angular Position Sensor Using Eddy Current Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The demands of contactless inductive angular position sensor using eddy current effect with high accuracy is growing with the explosive growth demands of new energy vehicle. The structure of magnetic field of the sensor was composed of a rotor with four blades, an excitation ring coil with two layers totaling 8 turns and two groups of sinusoidal receiving coils. The coil design principle and the electromagnetic induction theory of the inductive angular sensor were briefly described in this digest. The magnetic density in the air gaps and the induced voltages in the receiving coils were simulated by using finite element method. The simulated results were used to derive the angular error. A prototype of the inductive angular position sensor was manufactured. And an experimental platform was built to experimentally verify the simulated angular error.

articleTitle: Post-processing-based Flux-weakening Control of Variable Flux Reluctance Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel post-processing-based flux-weakening control method for variable flux reluctance machines. The proposed method achieves high-efficiency operation at elevated speeds by determining the optimal values for both ac- and de-field currents together with the commutation angle. The nonlinear electromagnetic characteristics of the benchmark variable flux reluctance machine are simulated to calculate torque production and back-EMF voltage in relation to the excitation parameters, namely, ac current, dc current, and commutation angle. The control algorithm determines the optimal values for these parameters to achieve the desired torque and speed references while minimizing the total excitation current.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Optimization Design of Axial-Flux Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine for Large-Capacity Flywheel Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Axial-flux permanent magnet synchronous machine (AFPMSM), with the advantages of high power density and compact structure, are suitable for large-capacity flywheel energy storage system (FESS). FESS is often used to improve efficiency as main development direction, while the traditional AFPMSM has the drawbacks of high loss and large cogging torque, which restricts the application of FESS. Therefore, the AFPMSM using soft magnetic composites (SMC) is proposed in this paper, then the parameters of machine are investigated, and finally a new optimization strategy combining back-propagation artificial neural network (BP-ANN) based on genetic algorithm (GA) and multi-objective particle swarm optimization (PSO) search algorithm is used for optimization design.

Author Keywords: axial-flux permanent magnet synchronous machine (A FPMSM)

articleTitle: Analytical Modeling and Dynamic Characterization of Radial Magnetic Couplings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Radial magnetic coupling (RMC) has many advantages as a contactless transmission device. However, RMCs are prone to pole-slipping, which needs to be avoided by studying the dynamic characteristics. To delve into the magnetic field model and dynamic characteristics of the RMC, a subdomain analytical method calculation model is employed to establish the transmission system simulation model of the RMC. Based on the transmission model, the dynamic characteristics of the RMC under different working conditions are analyzed. Subsequently, an experimental platform is constructed for the experimental verification of these dynamic characteristics.

articleTitle: Fast Analysis and Design for 3D-Structured Magnetic Components Using Surrogate Model from Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a new fast method to generate an accurate surrogate model for 3D-structured magnetic components using transfer learning (TL). By using the proposed TL method, the small amount of the training datasets obtained from the 3D finite element analysis is required for the accurate surrogate model. In this study, the surrogate models are constructed by the proposed and conventional models, and then the accuracy and number of the training datasets of the surrogate models are compared between two models to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Rigorous Treatment of Construction Imperfections in High-Frequency Microstrip EMC Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The versatile manipulation of fabrication faults in the design of microstrip EMC filters, is presented in this paper. To this objective, two accurate frequency-independent methods are developed. The first scheme obtains the roots of a new polynomial from a system of equations and the second one creates a compressed polynomial. Both approaches require that the maximum local peaks of the distorted original polynomial are smaller than unit. The proposed formulation is successfully certified via a 4th-order microstrip parallel coupled-line bandpass filter at 62 GHz.

articleTitle: A Topology Optimization of Electromagnetic Devices Based on Kernel Ridge Regression as a Variant of Gaussian Network-Based Shape Representation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a topology optimization method for electromagnetic devices based on Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR). As for this method, device shapes are represented through a response surface obtained by KRR. This method is a variant of the shape expression method based on Gaussian network-based approaches, nevertheless, it is shown that this method makes it possible to obtain more complicated shapes with better performance in comparison with the conventional method.

articleTitle: High-Speed Numerical Simulation of Shielding Current Analysis in Crack-Free HTS Thin Film: Improvement of ICCGH Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: By improving the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>-matrix-based preconditioning, the CG method with the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>-matrix-based acceleration technique (ICCGH method) has been modified. In addition, the performance of the modified ICCGH method has been evaluated numerically. The computation results show that the modified ICCGH method is faster than not only the standard CG method but also the conventional ICCGH method. It is concluded that the modified ICCGH method might be useful to speed up the shielding current analysis of the crack-free HTS thin film.

articleTitle: Comparative Research of Yokeless and Segmented Armature Axial Flux Motors with Surface-Mounted and Tangential Permanent Magnet Rotor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, two kinds of yokeless and segmented armature (YASA) motors are designed and compared. Firstly, a traditional surface-mounted YASA motor is designed in which a combined rotor disk is adopted. In order to reduce the eddy-current loss in the rotor and improve the performance of YASA motor, a tangential PM rotor structure is introduced. Then, the performances and eddy-current loss of YASA motors with two kinds of rotors are analyzed and compared. Finally, the prototype motors are manufactured for experimental research.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization of Microwave Devices with Thin Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a topology optimization of a microstrip bandpass filter based on the geometry projection method that can represent thin metals and air gaps. A population-based stochastic optimization algorithm is used to optimally place the rectangular air regions in the metal plate of a microwave filter. It is shown that the bandpass filter obtained by the proposed method, which has a thin stub, has a desired characteristic.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis for Long-Term Negative Discharges in Air with Needle-Plane Electrode Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this study, we investigate the partial discharge mechanism in needle electrodes under direct current (DC) voltage, with a focus on streamer propagation in atmospheric pressure air. Initially, we validated our numerical model by measuring current density at the ground electrode using a high-frequency current transformer (HFCT) and ultra-high frequency (UHF) sensor. In the extended study, we will compare the analysis results for different gaps between the needle electrode and the ground (5, 8, and 10 mm), adjusting the applied voltage from the partial discharge inception voltage to 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3 times the voltage level. We simultaneously conducted experimental and numerical analyses of the discharge current characteristics, focusing on five key parameters: rise time, decay time, maximum amplitude, pulse width, and pulse interval. Additionally, we investigated the long- term behavior of corona discharge using pulse sequence analysis (PSA) diagrams, aiming to apply these findings in real-world electrical equipment under operational conditions.

articleTitle: PEEC Based Fast 3D Litz Wire Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Litz wires, which are utilized to suppress eddy current, often have complex structures. This paper presents a partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC)-based 3D model for Litz wires with round conductor. The model accounts for both transverse and longitudinal magnetic fields. The discretization of the Litz wire is based on cylindrical elements resulting in a reduced number of elements. Cylindrical element analysis is based on a 2D analytical method. The proposed model is compared with 3D FEM, which shows the model has good accuracy and fast computational speed. It is promising to facilitate Litz wires optimization.

articleTitle: Permanent Magnet Motor Torque Waveform Prediction Using Learned Gap Flux
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a surrogate model based on neural networks, for the rapid evaluation of the performance of permanent magnet synchronous motor designs, especially the detailed torque waveform. In the training phase of our proposed method, motor design parameters are taken as input and gap flux density information is taken as output, both fed to train neural networks. In the test phase, gap flux density is predicted with the trained neural networks, the torque waveform is subsequently reconstructed, and a peak-to-peak cogging torque amplitude is estimated from the waveform. We compare the proposed method with conventional neural network based surrogate models, in which torque information is directly used for training, and confirm that the proposed method shows higher accuracy than conventional approaches, especially when the training data size is small.

articleTitle: Foil Winding Homogenization with Consideration of Capacitive Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The large number of turns in foil windings and the small thickness of the foil require many mesh elements in conventional finite element simulations. This renders models quickly computationally infeasible. With the use of homogenization approaches the small-scale structure in the foil winding domain does not not need to be resolved by the finite element mesh. Present homogenization approaches take resistive and inductive effects into account. With an increase of the operation frequency of foil windings, however, the capacitive effects between adjacent turns in the foil winding become relevant. This paper presents an extension to the standard foil winding model that covers these effects.

articleTitle: Ion Flow Field Numerical Simulation Method of High-Altitude UHVDC Transmission Lines Based on Weibull-WSE-UFEM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The ion flow field of UHVDC transmission lines is greatly affected by wind, especially in high-altitude areas where the regional and gradient differences in wind speed are significant. To accurately provide the required wind speed verification values for line parameter design, a numerical simulation method based on Weibull-WSE-UFEM is proposed in this paper. Weibull function is used to construct the probability distribution of wind speed in the studied area based on real data, and the maximum value within the appropriate range is selected as the wind speed verification value for the location of the wind speed sensor. Wind Shear Exponent (WSE) is used to expand the verification values at different positions in the vertical direction. Upstream Finite Element Method (UFEM) is used to calculate ion flow field and the verification values are used as the input wind speeds in different height nodes. The method was applied to a real high-altitude UHVDC transmission line case and the theoretical minimum height of line to ground was obtained. The results indicate that the method has certain guiding significance for the design of UHVDC transmission lines in high-altitude areas.

articleTitle: A Manufacturing Oriented Topology Optimization Methodology for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Numerous topology optimization (TO) investigations have been conducted to enhance the design of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM). Nevertheless, significant concerns persist regarding the manufacturability of the optimized outcomes. Substantial post-processing efforts are necessary to refine the optimized topology, particularly in dealing with zigzag boundaries, in order to prepare the design for the manufacturing. To eradicate the gap between the theoretically optimized model and the one for the engineering application, a manufacturing oriented TO approach for the PMSM is proposed. In particular, some elementary components are constructed and then evolved by using projective transformation and Boolean operations to generate new topologies. Numerical results validate the efficacy of this proposed approach in significantly improving the objective function while guaranteeing the manufacturability of the optimized outcomes.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Loop Magnetic Coil with High-Efficiency Wireless Charging and Attachment in Asymmetric Magnetic Latching System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Recently, research on applying a wireless charging system with magnetic latching has been conducted for alignment between wireless power transfer coils. However, magnets cause magnetic saturation in magnetic material due to DC field and deteriorate efficiency in wireless charging systems. This paper proposed a dual-loop magnetic coil to generate DC magnetic field for alignment without magnet and AC magnetic field for wireless power transfer in asymmetric magnetic latching system. The effectiveness of the proposed design was analyzed by comparing it with the WPT system with symmetric magnet in terms of circuit parameters. The proposed design is analyzed and verified through EM simulation.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Optimization Design of an AFFMPM Machine based on SVM and NSGA-II Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Axial-field flux-modulated permanent magnet (AFFMPM) motor combines the advantages of both axial-field (AF) topology and flux-modulation (FM) machine, which can improve torque density and achieve the characteristics of low speed and high torque. However, the special three-dimensional (3D) structure of AF topology results in time-consuming analysis of electromagnetic performance. Meanwhile, due to the strong coupling between FM machine parameters make the multi-objective and multi-parameter optimization necessary. This greatly intensifies the design and optimization cycle of AFFMPM machines. To address such issues, a multi-objective optimization design based on SVM and NSGA-II algorithm is proposed for the newly developed AFFMPM topology.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization of Magnetic Structure for Electromagnetic Force Maximization Supported by Error Correction Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In the design process of electrical machines, the accuracy of electromagnetic force calculation is needed to keep high for the minute design of electrical machines. The topology optimization (TO) combined with the high-accurate calculation of electromagnetic force can substantially improve the design quality of electrical machines. When the electromagnetic force is estimated using the finite element analysis, large numerical error is included under some conditions. As a result, non-physical magnetic structures were obtained in some cases of the TO. In this paper, to overcome the difficulty, the TO method supported by the error correction method of electromagnetic force was proposed, and its performance was verified.

articleTitle: Finite Element Models for High Voltage Cables with Large Cross Sections Using Dimensional Reduction and Homogenization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Segmented conductors are a common choice for high voltage cables with large copper cross sections. Their complex geometries lead to multi-scale problems when modeling their electromagnetic behaviour through eddy current boundary value problems. We propose an finite element model that combines advantages of certain coordinate transformations and homoge-nization techniques to make computational costs manageable.

articleTitle: Local Resistivity Model for Soft Magnetic Composite Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A resistivity model is proposed for soft magnetic composite materials. The model is complex-valued, but it has a time domain extension as a Cauer network. The model is expressed as a closed-form analytical expression. The resistivity depends explicitly on the physical and geometric properties of the material, and no empirical fitting parameters are introduced. Together with a similar kind of local reluctivity model, we find that a macroscale finite element model of a toroid is consistent with measurements. The presented methods provide a numerically efficient way to model soft magnetic composites.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Coupled Methodology for Calculation and Suppression of DC Bias in UHVDC Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In the field of Ultra High Voltage Direct Current (UHVDC) transmission, direct current (DC) bias currents can adversely affect the normal operation of transformers. This paper analyzes the computation of DC bias currents in a UHVDC system operating in monopolar mode with the earth serving as the return path. The indirect field-circuit coupling method proposed for calculating DC bias currents reduces the computation time to less than 1/20000 of that required by the direct coupling method used in commercial software, while ensuring accuracy. Based on this method, a multi-valued genetic algorithm is developed to optimize the configuration of DC bias resistive-capacitive suppression devices. This optimization reduces the demand for these devices by 23.9%, thus enhancing economic benefits and the potential for engineering applications.

articleTitle: A Study on the Comparison of Electromagnetic Design According to the Application of CFRP Sleeve to IPMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, we study the improvements in performance and manufacturability achieved by applying carbon fiber reinforced plastic (CFRP) to the rotor assembly of an interior permanent magnet synchronous motor. In order to reduce the mises stress of the rotor core, the dispersed design without CFRP sleeve model and the with CFRP sleeve model using only the CFRP sleeve are compared. Five models are analyzed for comparison. For the without CFRP sleeve model, it was tested at speeds of 30krpm, 27krpm, 24krpm, and 21krpm, and for the with CFRP sleeve model, it was tested at a speed of 30krpm. To satisfy the target parameters, which are the design goals of each model, design and analysis were performed by changing the number of turns and stack length. In addition, this paper examines the advantages of applying CFRP and predicts the cost for each model through volume calculation.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis of Surface and Space Charge with Floating Conductor under Dielectric Liquid Discharge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The dynamic characteristics of surface and space charge were analyzed under a dielectric liquid discharge with a floating conductor by use of a fully coupled finite element method. Until now, a liquid discharge analysis including a floating conductor has been rarely reported with a generalized three carriers such as electron, and positive and negative ions as unknown variables. We, here, built up three carrier system with a floating conductor where a liquid discharge happens. To verify our numerical setup, first, the unipolar space charge propagation was analyzed and compared to those from a theory with a linear charge injection. In an extended paper, we will show more real analysis setup with three carriers for discharge analysis combined with a floating conductor as an obstacle.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization of an IPMSM Rotor Considering the Torque Profile Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To extend the automatic design process of the interior permanent magnet synchronous motors (IPMSM), a density-based topology optimization approach of the rotor is developed in this research. Considering the torque performance as the objective, the topology optimization is conducted under the constraint of the mechanical performance and electromagnetic performance including the structural strength and the torque ripple respectively. A validation example of an IPMSM is used to prove the effectiveness of the developed optimization.

articleTitle: Identification of an Arbitrary-Surface Harmonic Magnetic Model from Close Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Decreasing spherical harmonic functions are widely used to identify and extrapolate the magnetic field produced by various devices. These functions are equivalent to a multipolar decomposition which orders the field according to its spatial decreasing rate. However this representation is not valid inside the Brillouin sphere, the smallest sphere enclosing the device. We introduce here the use of an alternative representation to replace the spherical harmonic functions when the measurement are inside the Brillouin sphere. This representation uses a basis of equivalents charges on a surface to reproduce the multipolar decomposition while being valid inside the Brillouin sphere. We demonstrate here the ability of this model to identify and extrapolate the field from very close measurements.

articleTitle: Nondestructive Estimation of Permanent Magnet Magnetization Using Measured Value of Leakage Flux Originating from PMSM Rotor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Manufacturing mass-produced machines of the permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) include post-assembly magnetization process. Because the performance of PMSMs depends on the quality of permanent magnets (PMs), the estimation of PM magnetization is important process. Several magnetization estimation methods for pre-assembly magnetization have been proposed. However, no method for post-assembly magnetization had been proposed to estimate the magnetization distribution, which includes the magnetic nonlinearity of the magnetic circuit. In this paper, the magnetization estimation method using the Leakage flux derived from the magnetic circuit (MELF) is proposed. The performance of the proposed method (MELF) is verified using actual rotor of IEEJ D-model which is one of the benchmarks PMSMs.

articleTitle: A Domain Decomposition Finite Element Method for the Magneto-Thermal Field Analysis of Electric Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a domain decomposition finite element method is proposed for the magneto-thermal field analysis of electric machines. 2-D and 3-D numerical models are built for the magnetic field and thermal field of electric machines, respectively. The computational domains of these two fields are decomposed into subdomains based on the discretized meshes to balance the computation work between processors. With the decomposed subdomains, the additive Schwarz method is developed to solve the forming numerical problems of these two fields using the open source platform freefem++, and a significant improvement in efficiency can be observed from the numerical results of single field analysis of a permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM). The coupling between these two fields is modelled with the electromagnetic losses and temperature dependent properties, and a two-step searching algorithm is developed for the data mapping between field solvers, which employ different dimensional models and inconsistent meshes. The counterpart subdomain is determined before searching the counterpart element to reduce the computation effort of searching. The magneto-thermal field analysis of the studied PMSM is finally conducted with the proposed method to showcase its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Magnetic Property Calibration for Vibrating Sample Magnetometers Based on Magnetic Field Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This study proposes a method for the calibration of vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM), designed to compensate for the effects of internal demagnetizing field. This method utilizes finite element calculations and evolutionary search to find the optimal demagnetizing factor. This method has been validated to exhibit higher accuracy than existing methods, and the calibrated magnetic property aligns well with the results obtained through the capacitive cancellation method.

articleTitle: Measurement Uncertainty of Schumann Resonances with the EFIELD Experiment on Board Dragonfly
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: EFIELD sensors on board the Geophysical and Meteorological package (DraGMet) of the NASA Dragonfly mission will passively record the time-varying electrical field on Saturn's largest moon: Titan. The main goal of these sensors is to detect Schumann Resonances (SR), which propagates between the ionized atmospheric layer and a subsurface layer, presumably a salty water ocean. Measuring these electromagnetic resonances allows us to determine the characteristics of the cavity and especially the ocean depth, which is crucial to assess the habitability of Titan. This work describes the analytical developments and numerical simulations we performed to assess the measurement uncertainty of the EFIELD probes.

articleTitle: Simplified Optimization of Curved Barrier in Synchronous Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: One of the most important things to maximize the performance of synchronous reluctance motor is to optimize the shape of a rotor. In this paper, two techniques are proposed for changing the rotor barrier curved with only one parameter. The first is to use the curve graph of the power function, and the second is to use the curve graph of the exponential function. Finally, the optimum points of the parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> of the two techniques are suggested and the torque performance resulting from the optimized design is analyzed for evaluating the techniques.

articleTitle: Calculation of Ion Flow Field of HVDC Lines Considering the Influence of Stochastic Suspended-Particles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The charged suspended-particle around HVDC lines will affect the ion flow density and electric field (ion flow field), however, the charging model of the suspended-particle considering the distribution characteristics is not well studied. In this paper, the stochastic-distribution model of the suspended-particle charge density is developed, which is fully included in the calculation of ion flow field. After the validity of the proposed stochastic model is verified by experiment results, the ion flow field under ± 800kV HVDC lines in the polluted environment is analyzed by using upstream finite element method, and statistical parameters are obtained.

articleTitle: Surrogate Model-Based Synthesis of NFC-Transponders
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Independent of the respective NFC (near field communication) application the specific NFC device has to be tested for standard compliance. In the present work we propose a hybrid surrogate-model based synthesis strategy which enables the incorporation of standard compliance tests in the synthesis process. While the surrogate model is used in early optimization phases applying a stochastic optimization strategy, the highfidelity model is applied in the final deterministic optimization part. The high fidelity model is based on a thin wire partial element equivalent circuit method.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Analysis and Calculation of Slotless Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Motor with Sinusoidal Back EMF
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: For slotless axial flux permanent magnet motor (AFPM), the 3-D finite element method is the most accurate design approach, but it suffers from long computational time. To address this issue, this paper proposes an analytical design method for slotless AFPM with sinusoidal back EMF. Initially, the open-circuit electromotive force (EMF) of AFPM with toroidal and bunched winding is derived using the winding function method. Subsequently, a 3-D analytical model for the magnetic field of AFPM with sinusoidal back EMF is established, with a detailed analysis of the air-gap density. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated by comparing the results with those obtained from finite element methods.

Author Keywords: Axial flux permanent magnet synchronous motor

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Topology Optimization of Synchronous Reluctance Motor with Autoencoder Simultaneously Considering Material Selection and Shape Change
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Generally, the optimal shape depends on the characteristics of the magnetic materials used. In this study, we propose an efficient multi-objective topology optimization method that simultaneously considers material selection and shape change. The proposed approach utilizes an Autoencoder, a type of deep learning model, to compress the information of both the device's shape and material characteristics into a latent space. The method enables us to efficiently derive superior combinations of shapes and materials for improving device's performances as pareto solutions. Some numerical examples demonstrate we can successfully carry out the practical device design by combining the proposed approach with the level set method.

articleTitle: Power Transmission Characteristics Analysis of Multi-port Dual-Flux-Modulator Magnetic Geared Machine Based on Analytical Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents an effective analytical model of Dual-Flux-Modulator Magnetic Geared Machine which considers the slotting effect of the main and auxiliary flux modulators. The power transmission characteristics of each port in DFM-MGM are analyzed. The finite element method (FEM) and experiments are used to verify the correctness of the presented analytical model.

articleTitle: An Auxiliary Differential Equation–Finite Element Method for 3D Transient Simulation of Currents in HVDC Insulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Insulation is a crucial component for High Voltage electric equipment such as HVDC power cables. The accurate estimation of the electric stresses to which the insulation material is exposed in both transient and steady state conditions is of great importance for cable design and rating as well as for lifetime estimation. We present an Auxiliary Differential Equation–Finite Element Method (ADE–FEM) numerical model for the computation of transient electric field and currents in 3D insulation materials. The method is based on a formulation that uses (scalar) polarization charges rather that polarization vectors as unknowns in order to reduce the computational complexity, and on a space of low order hierarchical basis functions that allow for efficient local grid refinement.

articleTitle: Structural Optimization and Simulation Analysis of Orthogonal Controllable Reactors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Orthogonal controllable reactors have the advantages of low harmonic content and relatively linear inductance change, and have a wide application prospect in power supply management and other fields. In response to the requirements of a certain project, this article optimizes the structure of the orthogonal controllable reactor by adding a air gap between the AC core and DC core, and analyzes the magnetic circuit of the magnetically controlled region after this kind of structural optimization. The simulation and experimental results show that the optimized orthogonal controllable reactor has a inductance regulation range of 56% and its harmonic content is low.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulations of Semiconductor Structures at Highest Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To describe the charge transport in semiconductor topologies, the drift-diffusion model (DDM) and the hydrodynamic model (HDM) have been widely used. In this work, within the framework of DDM, a numerical solver has been realized, based on the continuous Galerkin finite element method (FEM). The analysis is conducted for a n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>nn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> structure, using a voltage source excitation. For verifying the obtained results, a commercialized software tool has been employed as a reference. This tool has been also used to simulate HDM for the studied structure. It is demonstrated that the DDM solvers agree closely. As a next step, an HDM solver is currently developed for revealing additional features of the above topology, invisible for DDM. This solver will incorporate both the continuous and discontinuous Galerkin FEM, for accuracy and efficiency comparisons.

articleTitle: Complementary Formulations for Electroquasistatics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In static electromagnetic problems, complementarity provides upper and lower energetic bounds, the presence of which has been thoroughly studied and justified. This is not the case for quasistatic problems, for which the presence of these bounds has only been shown numerically for the magnetoquasistatic case. In this work we investigate whether or not these bounds are present in the electroquasistatic hypothesis.

articleTitle: Structural and Analytical Modeling of a Long Stroke Variable Stiffness Magnetic Spring with Application to Wave Energy Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a new structure of long-stroke variable stiffness magnetic spring (MS) applied to wave energy converter device is proposed, and the corresponding analytical model (AM) is presented according to its structure. The main part of the MS consists of an inner mover, an outer stator and a back iron, and the main part is connected to a stepper motor through a shaft, and the stepper motor rotates the intermediate shaft so as to control the change of the stiffness of the MS. The simulated stroke of the MS is 120mm and the maximum elasticity is about 1.7kN. Then an AM combining surface current method and equivalent magnetic circuit method is proposed for the structure of MS. The accuracy of the AM can be verified by comparing the AM with the finite element method (FEM).

articleTitle: A $\boldsymbol{T}, \Phi-\Phi$ Multiscale Finite Element Formulation for Eddy Current Problems in Open Magnetic Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The multiscale finite element method has shown its high potential for the simulation of the eddy current problem in closed magnetic circuits with laminated cores. This work presents a new approach developed to extend the multiscale finite element method to open magnetic circuits. To this end, a three dimensional eddy current problem with the novel <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{T},\Phi- \Phi$</tex> multiscale formulation and linear material relations has been studied. Numerical results demonstrate the high accuracy of the presented method.

articleTitle: Acceleration of Waveform Control for Measurement of Magnetic Hysteresis Based on Single Sheet Tester Using Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In recent years, the high-quality design of various motors to realize high efficiency is enthusiastically demanded owing to the promotion of electric vehicles. Therefore, it is essential to accurately evaluate of the motor design using the finite element analysis. Furthermore, the accurate measurement data of magnetic property obtained employing the single sheet tester (SST) is also required. However, when the measurement of magnetic hysteresis under the condition that high magnetic flux density on the low-frequency region is operated, the number of feedback iterations for the flux waveform control tends to increase owing to the excess distortion of the excitation voltage waveform. Consequently, since the elapsed time for the measurement also tends to increase, the development of a method to reduce the elapsed time is substantially required. In this paper, to reduce the elapsed time for the measurement of the magnetic hysteresis, the convergence characteristics of the flux waveform control are accelerated by the estimation of the initial waveform of the excitation voltage waveform using a neural network (NN).

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of A Hybrid Excitation Electromagnetic Lead Screw Based on the Equivalent Magnetic Circuit Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a magnetic equivalent circuit is proposed to improve the analysis accuracy and reduce the computation time of the hybrid excitation electromagnetic lead screw (HEMLS). The magnetic field distribution and the performance of the HEMLS can be analyzed by the proposed model. Finally, the calculation results are compared with the finite element method to verify the correctness of the proposed equivalent magnetic circuit method.

articleTitle: Study on Arc Diagnostic Device for 1000V Class Electric Vehicle Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This study analyzed the necessity of applying a DC arc fault detection device to diagnose DC arcs that may occur in the line between the battery and inverter. The arc voltage and arc power characteristics according to arc current were analyzed through constructing a 1000V, 400A battery bank and arc generator. The time required for actual arc diagnosis or blocking when using full load was figured out by using the Paukert V-I equation.

articleTitle: Zero-Order Electromagnetic Vibration Reduction Method for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor With Harmonic Currents Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: With the widespread application of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs), their vibration and noise have also received more attention. The traditional reducing vibration method by adjusting the motor topology is not universal and costly. Because the zero-order mode of PMSMs often have low natural frequency, it is one of the key factors causing motor vibration. Therefore, a method of reducing the zero-order component of electromagnetic force waves by injecting harmonic currents is proposed in this paper. Based on the zero-order modal frequencies of different PMSMs, the method can reduce electromagnetic vibration by flexibly changing the frequency and amplitude of harmonic currents.

articleTitle: Evolution and Comparison of Two Axial–Flux PM Machines for all–Electric Aircraft Propulsion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposed, optimized and compared two dual–rotor axial–flux permanent magnet (PM) machines for all–electric aircraft (AEA) propulsion. Several features, including the Halbach array and PM skewing, are introduced to improve power density and efficiency. To reduce the computational burden of finite element analysis, the surrogate modals of machines are constructed by Box–Behnken design. Then, the electromagnetic performances, such as induced voltage, torque characters and efficiency of the proposed machines are simulated. It is shown that the YASA machine is a superior choice for AEA propulsion due to its higher output torque, power density, torque density and efficiency when compared to the AFVPM machine.

articleTitle: Multi-Level Optimization Based on Approximate Models for Double-Sided Linear Flux Switching Permanent Magnet Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel multi-level optimization method for DLFSPM is proposed, to improve the efficiency of multi-objective optimization. To split the high dimension parameters space, a combination of comprehensive sensitivity analysis, correlation analysis, and cross-factor variance analysis is employed to evaluate the effect of the machine's structure parameters towards the optimization objective. Moreover, an approximate model for this machine based on BOHB-RF and a least squares method of approximation is applied to reduce the computational complexity for motor modeling. Then, Nondominated sorting genetic algorithm-II (NSGA-II) is applied to optimize the DLFSPM with a level-by-level multi-objective optimization design, that to obtain the global optimal performance of this motor with high thrust density, low thrust ripple and low mover loss. Finally, the results of FEA prove the effectiveness for the multi-level optimization method.

articleTitle: Multi-physics Analysis and Optimal Design of an Outer Rotor Surface Mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor for Coaxial Drone
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper deals with the multi-physics analysis and optimal design of an outer rotor surface mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor for coaxial drones. The propulsion system of a coaxial drone has a structure in which the top propeller, top motor, inverter, bottom motor, and bottom propeller are arranged at short intervals on one vertical axis, which has the advantages of compact size compared to multi-copter drones and high safety in unstable airflow. However, there is a disadvantage that there is almost no airflow between the upper and lower propellers during operation, so the motors and inverter located in that position are not well cooled. This disadvantage can cause demagnetization of permanent magnets and deterioration of windings due to temperature rise inside the motor during operation. Therefore, motors for coaxial drones need to have stable thermal characteristics. They also need to have a high specific power to reduce the Maximum Take-Off Weight (MTOW) of coaxial drones. To achieve these goals, multi-physics analysis of the motor, i.e., electromagnetic, thermal, and mechanical analysis, is essential. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-physics analysis and optimal design process of an outer rotor surface mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor for coaxial drones, and based on it, performs multi-physics analysis and optimal design of motor. The multi-physics analysis of the motor is performed based on finite element analysis, Computational Fluid Dynamics(CFD), and thermal equivalent circuit method, and the optimal design of the motor is performed using the Response Surface Method(RSM) considering the results of the multi-physics analysis. Finally, the final model resulting from the optimal design is manufactured, and experiments are conducted to verify the validity of the multi-physics analysis and optimal design results.

articleTitle: Design Consideration of a Permanent Magnet Assist Synchronous Reluctance Motor used in Oil-Submersible Electric Pump System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Ferrite has the advantages of low price and positive temperature coefficient of coercivity. Therefore, ferrite based submersible permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance motor (SPMA-SynRM) can be an optional topology for oil-submersible electric pump. This paper analyzed the requirements in submersible motor and the suitability of PMA-SynRM, and designed a SPMA-SynRM based on the finite element method (FEM). The single-layer winding and parallel slots are adopted in stator to improve the empirical slot fill factor, and the triple-layer U-type flux barriers with ferrite are adopted in rotor to improve the saliency ratio and torque. Furthermore, this paper compared its cost and performance with PMSM. Finally, the maximum rotor stress, the anti-demagnetization performance of the ferrite and the steady-state temperature rise of the motor were also calculated in this paper.

Author Keywords: submersible permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance motor (SPMA-SynRM)

articleTitle: Interior Penalty Galerkin Methods for Time Domain Eddy Current Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes the family of interior penalty methods to solve an eddy current problem in the time domain. These methods use discontinuous basis functions to approximate the solution and penalize the jump of the solution by introducing an additional term. Using discontinuous basis functions and applying Galerkin's method leads to a block-diagonal mass matrix in conducting regions, which can be inverted easily. Therefore, an explicit time-stepping scheme can be used. Depending on the considered problem, the numerical scheme in the conducting region can be coupled with classical finite elements in the nonconducting region or described by an interior penalty method as well. The theory of the methods is illustrated by assuming the A-A formulation for a two-dimensional problem,

articleTitle: Dual Inverter Parallel Consequent Pole PM-Assisted Two-Layer Sub-Harmonic Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A parallel consequent pole PM-assisted 2-layer subharmonic machine consisting of dual inverter topology is proposed here, which is designed to enhance torque generation and control compared to its predecessors. The stator of the sub-harmonic synchronous machine has two sets of 3-phase windings, and the dual inverter supplies current to them separately. Similarly, the rotor has two concentric windings, one for field excitation and the other for harmonic excitation. To validate the proposed model, an 8-pole, 48-slot, 2-inverter, 2-layer sub-harmonic machine is designed and simulated through 2-D finite element analysis. The results show a better torque and performance than the subharmonic and wound field synchronous machines.

articleTitle: A Novel Electromagnetic Voltage Transformer Based on Magnetic Valve
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Voltage transformers are crucial components of power systems, which serve various purposes. However, traditional electromagnetic voltage transformers suffer from saturation issues due to the presence of magnetic cores. It can result in inaccurate voltage measurements, overheating, or damage to the transformer. Meanwhile, it can even pose risks to the power system due to ferroresonance. In this paper, a novel electromagnetic voltage transformer utilizing a magnetic valve is proposed, which is capable of compensating for distorted voltage after saturation and extending the measuring range. The anti-DC bias capability of the proposed voltage transformer is improved by including a magnetic valve and magnetic field sensor. Finite element simulations and prototype experiments verified the correctness of the proposed transformer's principle.

articleTitle: Modeling of a Winding by Segmentation and a Two Domain Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Passive filters in power electronics often use in-ductances made of a winding with a ferrite core. Brute force finite element modeling of a thin wire and a small penetration depth may become rather expensive or practically impossible. Therefore, the entire winding is assumed to be decomposed into segments to allow a feasible modeling. A two-domain method is considered using an obvious basis for the electromagnetic field inside the wire segment and the finite element method outside. The skin effect and proximity effect are considered properly. A numerical example with a straight wire segment shows satisfactory results.

articleTitle: Adaptive Local Mesh Refinement for Steady State and Transient Simulation of Semiconductor Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: We propose an adaptive non-conforming mesh refinement technique for two dimensional semiconductor device simulation on triangular meshes to increase the numerical accuracy in regions of interest. To capture the solution with large gradient in thin layers, three physics-based cell refinement indicators are proposed to effectively locate critical areas around junctions, electrodes and the boundaries of space charge regions respectively. The local conservation property of finite volume Scharfetter-Gummel scheme is preserved after refinement by proper control volume discretization and interpolation rule even with hanging nodes. Steady state and transient simulation results showed that the meshes are properly refined and the numerical error is reduced.

articleTitle: Development of MR-Sensor-Based Measurement System for Weak Magnetic Field Derived From Fuel Cell and its Application to Inverse Estimation of Current Density Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The increasing demand for systems capable of estimating the performance of polymer electrolyte fuel cells during operation has highlighted the need for nondestructive methods to assess their dynamic behavior. This is particularly important for evaluating changes in current density (CD), a key factor affecting fuel cell sustainability and performance. Our study addresses this need by developing a nondestructive CD estimation system. It includes a highly accurate MR-sensor-based measurement system for measuring the weak magnetic field generated by the current in the fuel cell, coupled with a numerical estimation method that leverages the measurement data. This approach promises significant advancements in the sustainable and high-performance operation of fuel cells.

articleTitle: An Improved Method for Electromagnetic Calculations of Dynamically Varying Cantilever Beam RF-MEMS Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a numerical method based on finite difference time domain (FDTD) method is provided for analyzing electromagnetic characteristics of RF-MEMS switch with a dynamic cantilever beam in presence. The basic idea is transforming the original dynamic boundary problem to a static one via the map between two frames, one is the realistic physic frame and the other is the imaginary reference frame in which the beam is stationary. Under such a transformation, the FDTD-like time-marching scheme is formulated. The suggested method is then applied in a specific case for validation.

articleTitle: Performance Prediction Process of Outer Rotor PMSM Through 3-D Flux Coefficient Using Equivalent 2-D FEA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this article, we propose an equivalent 2-D finite element analysis (FEA) process considering the 3-D flux of an outer rotor permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). In motor, 3-D flux such as axial leakage flux (ALF) and overhang fringing flux (OFF) are influenced based on design variables. 3-D FEA is required to consider the components of 3-D flux. However, 3-D FEA is inefficient to use during the design process because of time-consuming. Therefore, we propose an equivalent FEA that considers 3-D flux. First, the effects of ALF and OFF according to design variables such as rotor inner and outer diameter, stack length, and overhang length. Second, the 3-D flux is converted into coefficient. Finally, it is applied to 2-D FEA. Using the proposed process, motor performance considering 3-D flux can be quickly predicted. The proposed performance prediction process is verified through simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: New BH Curve Tracking Method Based on Magnetic Contact Force
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a method that utilizes magnetic contact force to track the BH curve of electrical steel. Typically, the BH curve of electrical steel is measured using an Epstein frame or a vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM). However, the Epstein frame faces challenges in measuring at high magnetic field levels, and VSMs can be costly. The method proposed in this study tracks the internal flux density and magnetic field strength of the sample by utilizing magnetic contact force between the core and the sensor. The core and the sample are configured within a simple closed-loop magnetic circuit. Consequently, it becomes possible to generate high magnetic fields with minimal energy, enabling cost-effective miniaturization. To validate this, an electromagnet model was constructed for comparative analysis.

articleTitle: Coupled Electromagnetic-Fluid- Thermal Analysis in Large Scale Water-Hydrogen-Hydrogen Cooled Generator-Condenser Under Different Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this article, the electromagnetic performance and stator thermal field of the 350MW/300Mvar water-hydrogen-hydrogen-cooled generator-condenser under different operating conditions are compared and analyzed by electromagnetic-fluid-thermal coupling model. The calculation results from the two-dimensional field-circuit model and the global ventilation network serve as coupling boundary conditions for the solid-fluid solution domain. The conclusions drawn provide useful references for the design and renovation of this type of generator-condenser.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic-Mechanical Model Consideration of High-Speed Train High Voltage Traction Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This work proposes an electromagnetic-mechanical modeling of an interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) as a traction motor for high-speed railway traction application. Based on initial modeling, mechanical model modifications are proposed that can improve the overall robustness of the traction motor.

articleTitle: Fatigue Propagation Analysis of Crack Failure in High Power IGBT Solder Based on Multiphysics Coupling Model and XFEM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: IGBT is one of the most important power modules in the electric traction converter system. In the long-term operation of the converter system, the IGBT module will suffer from alternating thermal load, frequent vibration impact and other coupling effects, which will easily lead to the cracking of the solder layer and the change of material properties, and the aging and damage of the accelerator parts. In this paper, the thermal-mechanical coupling finite element analysis model is established, and the influence of temperature on material properties is considered. The crack damage and periodic fatigue propagation behavior of solder layer are analyzed. Based on the damage mechanics theory and Paris equation, the fatigue propagation characteristics of IGBT solder layer crack element under periodic coupling stress are studied by using the extended finite element method, and the coupling effects of transient temperature change and vibration impact load on the dynamic crack propagation and damage aging evolution of IGBT solder layer under the change of material properties caused by temperature are considered.

articleTitle: Novel Microspeaker Design for Smartwatches with Integrated Woofer and Tweeter Units
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Addressing the escalating demand for superior performance in wearable devices, this study presents a novel microspeaker design tailored for smartwatches, incorporating integrated woofer and tweeter units. Employing the Electromagnetic-Mechanical-Acoustic (E-M-A) coupling method, the study analyzes the force factor and sound pressure level (SPL). Through the examination of the novel microspeaker design, the operation of two coils independently demonstrates a considerable enhancement in SPL, particularly in the mid-frequency range.
