Notably, the novel microspeaker design exhibits results comparable to those of the prototype.

articleTitle: A Vector Extension of the D-D-D Hysteresis Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper delves with the hysteresis modeling of magnetic materials. Recently, a scalar phenomenological model, referred to as D-D-D model, has been developed by the authors. In this study, an extension to vector hysteresis modeling is proposed.

articleTitle: Motor Characteristics Map Prediction Using Deep Operator Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A novel deep learning model that predicts motor characteristics using a deep operator network and convolutional neural networks is proposed. The proposed method accurately predicts motor characteristics under various currents and rotation angles. The proposed method improves the prediction accuracy by 43.5% compared to the conventional method.

articleTitle: Modeling and Experimental Verification of Multilayer Winding Method for the Vibration Improvement of Electric Motor With Sub-Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Fractional slot concentrated winding synchronous motor has great electrical properties such as high torque density, low cogging torque, and low torque ripple. However severe vibration is caused by sub-harmonics which are below the fundamental harmonic order in magnetomotive force (MMF). In this paper, four-layer winding is proposed to the motor design for sub-harmonics reduction instead of two-layer winding because sub-harmonics are affected by the ratio of armature winding and magnet field. To prevent the four-layer winding from lowering electromagnetic characteristics, a discrete design optimization is performed. Finally, to verify the proposed method, two motors of 12 -slot/10pole with four-layer winding and two-layer winding are manufactured and their performances are compared.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness Evaluation of Wall-Integrated Energy Storage Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A homogenisation procedure of capacitor-based energy storage devices is described with the aim of calculating their shielding effectiveness to the electromagnetic waves when they are installed inside building walls. The capacitors of the individual modules have a multilayered structure, in which the layers have very small thicknesses. Therefore, an analytical method based on multi-section transmission lines has been applied, establishing an analytical fast and consistent methodology that leads to a straightforward evaluation of the shielding capabilities.

articleTitle: Elliptical Loop-Microstrip Array for Focus Brain Lobe Imaging with 11.74 Teslas MRI System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging MRI, is a medical modality to acquire anatomical and functional images of the human body. The advantage of acquiring images with high definition is an important trait for diagnosis, therapy planning and understanding the body metabolism. The image resolution and signal-to-noise ratio SNR of MRI depends on the strength of the static magnetic field B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. With the recent development at our site of a 11.74 Teslas (T) MRI scanner for human imaging, we are preparing for novel RF transmission and reception coils brain imaging. In this work, we propose the use of a modification of a microstrip in the shape of an elliptical loop, and extended to an array structure to deliver magnetic |B1|-field into a brain model.

articleTitle: Toward the Modeling of Thin Conductive Layer With Hybrid FDTD-PITD Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A novel hybrid algorithm is proposed to model the embedded thin conductive layer (TCL). The finite-difference time-domain method is adopted for coarse grids outside TCL and the precise-integration time-domain method for one-dimensional fine grids inside TCL, synchronously updating the fields of different grids. Numerical results confirm the efficiency and accuracy of the new hybrid method.

articleTitle: Calculation of Iron Loss in Soft Magnetic Composites Using Neural Network-Based Dynamic Hysteresis Model Under SVPWM Excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Soft Magnetic Composite (SMC) materials, serving as key components in high-power motors, exhibit a loss mechanism distinctly different from traditional laminated core materials like silicon steel. To predict these losses more accurately, this study introduces a dynamic hysteresis model based on Neural Networks (NN) and trapezoidal equivalent circuits, designed to calculate the iron losses of SMC under Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (SVPWM) excitation. A NN algorithm, capable of characterizing the magnetization process, simulates the static hysteresis component. Meanwhile, when calculating eddy current losses and anomalous losses using trapezoidal equivalent circuits, the effect of skin effect on iron losses is taken into account. The model's accuracy and effectiveness are validated through a comparison of theoretical and experimental results. This model enhances the application of SMC in motors and provides robust support for the optimization of motor design.

Author Keywords: Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation excitation

articleTitle: Design of a Low-Cost PM Vernier Machine with Improved Electromagnetic Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: By utilizing various design techniques this paper aims to improve the electromagnetic performance of a ferrite based consequent pole PM Vernier machine (CP-PMVM). CP-PMVM with thick ferrite PMs offers considerable reluctance torque while having the advantage of reduced PM cost. However, CP structure suffers from the torque ripple issue, moreover its power factor is exceptionally low. Those issues can be resolved by adapting various design techniques such as controlling the, stator / rotor tooth fillet, symmetric / asymmetric PM pole arc ratio / PM thickness, flux gaps in stator. Mostly, various design techniques have contradictory effects on the electromagnetic performance thus improving the overall machine performance by having the best compromise is quite challenging. To demonstrate various aspects of the design problem, the detailed electromagnetic performance of a prototype CP-PMVM with variation of the key design parameters have been investigated in detail. The further extensions of the idea will be detailed in the full paper.

articleTitle: Effect of Anisotropic Localization in a Ferroelectric Multiscale Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, the effect of various localization rules in a ferroelectric multiscale model is studied. Ferroelectric materials are highly heterogeneous materials which means local fields vary from grain to grain. Many localization rules can be used in multiscale models to consider for this heterogeneity. In this paper, 3 localization rules are implemented providing results which are compared and analyzed.

articleTitle: Dynamic Process Modeling in Induction Heating Considering Temperature-Dependent Magnetic Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Owing to the temperature-dependent magnetic properties, steel sheets undergo a dynamic process of eddy current and temperature variation. Accurate modeling is important for the effective control of the heating process. In this study, magnetic-thermal coupled analysis is employed to examine the temperature distribution in steel sheets and the consequential impact of edge effects. The research accounts for the temperature-dependent magnetic properties of steel, establishing a dynamic process for the temperature changes in steel sheets over a detailed time series.

articleTitle: Reduced Order Modeling of Rectangular Wires in a Magneto-quasi-static Field for Integral Formulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach based on the Cauer ladder network method to calculate the complex permeability of a rectangular wire, which is a key ingredient of the integral equation formulation. The proposed method has equivalent accuracy but lower computational cost and memory requirements with respect to the standard finite element method, which is the current method of choice for the same computation.

articleTitle: Implementation of an Anisotropic Magnetic Model Based on the Effective Field in a Finite Element Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The magnetic anisotropic of steel sheets tends to increase the core losses and the magnetizing current of electric machines. Their accurate evaluation can adjust the machine design to improve the machine performances. Whereas various non-linear magnetic anisotropic models can represent the material behavior properly, their implementation into finite element requires the magnetic model to be derived from a thermodynamic potential. In this article, we implement the anisotropic model based on the effective field into a finite element model.

articleTitle: Efficient Digital Twin of SPM based on FEA enabling Drive Current Harmonics Elimination
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The paper proposes an efficient methodology for digital twin construction of surface mounted synchronous permanent magnet motors enabling current harmonics elimination under PWM inverter supply. The method is based on finite element analysis of various motor operating conditions and determination of appropriate variable lumped parameter motor dynamic model. Both space harmonics and armature reaction impact on local saturation are taken into consideration. This technique achieves substantial torque ripple reduction and losses decrease. The method introduced has been validated by measurements on a manufactured prototype motor drive system.

articleTitle: Calculation and Experimental Study of Floating Potential on Metal Shielding in Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Safety and efficiency are paramount in wireless power transfer systems. Floating potential and free charges are detected on the metal shielding layer when the system was charging, which are the safety hazards. To quantify the floating potential of WPT system, the numerical calculation method and the influencing factors of the potential were studied. The equivalent circuit considering the ferrite-aluminum plate composite shielding structure is firstly modelled and the resonant voltages on the coil are calculated by finite elements. The capacitive voltage from the metal shielding to the ground is also calculated under the equivalent electric quasi-static field. The effects of the frequency of the coupling mechanism, axial distance, and radial distance on the floating potential are analyzed lastly. To verify the numerical calculation reliability, a wireless charging platform was constructed and the floating potential were measured and analyzed. The results showed the calculation is agreement with measurement, which validate the accuracy and viability of the numerical calculation method. The proposed method is useful to calculate the floating potential and optimize the metal shielding in wireless power transfer system.

articleTitle: Analytical Approach of Sideband Electromagnetic Vibration of PMSM Driven by Voltage Source Inverter With SVPWM Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The research on the characteristics of sideband harmonic currents would provide guidance for the electromagnetic force wave, vibration, and acoustic noise of the motor. In this paper, the main components of sideband harmonic currents in a PMSM driven by the SVPWM strategy are analytically derived. An experimental test of an 8-pole/48-slot interior PMSM fed by a voltage source inverter with SVPWM is carried out, and the phase stator currents, vibration response, and acoustic noise signals are collected. The results verify the accuracy of the derivation analysis of sideband currents and indicate the relationship between sideband harmonic currents and electromagnetic vibration, providing a reference for further studies on vibration suppression.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Design Optimization of a PMSG Using a Deep Neural Network Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This digest presents the design optimization of a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) based on machine learning. A deep neural network (DNN) was developed using 3D FE data of a PMSG. The DNN is based on the nonlinear Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU). The resulting DNN was later used to construct the PMSG objective function which was then minimized. Numerical results are given.

articleTitle: Physics-Informed Neural Network for 2D Magneto-Quasi-Static Problems in Time Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) is proposed to solve 2D magneto-quasi-static (MQS) problems in time domain. Instead of discretization or interpolation in space and time, our method encodes the initial and boundary conditions as well as governing equations into loss function of PINN to optimize it. By comparing the PINN and finite element method (FEM) results, it shows that the PINN with limited number of layers and neurons in each layer can predict the magnetic field with relatively high accuracy after training.

articleTitle: A Modified Fixed-Point Iteration Algorithm for Magnetic Field Computation with Hysteresis Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A modified fixed-point iteration algorithm is proposed for electromagnetic finite element analysis with a hysteretic material model. In this method, the convergence factor is dynamically adjusted at each time step based on the specific situation. It has been verified that this approach improves computational speed and stability in solving nonlinear hysteresis electromagnetic simulation problems.

articleTitle: A Magneto-Elastic Vector-Play Model Under Rotating Fields and Multiaxial Stress States
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The hysteresis behavior of ferromagnetic materials under stress is represented using an energy-based vector-play approach combined with a multiscale model. A mathematical adaption of the pinning parameter allows capturing the vanishing of hysteresis losses under a rotating field near saturation. Using parameters identified from uniaxial measurements only, the modeling results agree well with the measured hysteresis loops under multiaxial mechanical loadings and rotating fields. The hysteresis loss trend under stress is also reproduced with the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Data-driven finite element mesh generation expert system based on BP neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper establishes a fully connected neural network to determine the finite element mesh density. Given an initial mesh in the domain to be solved, the mesh density is obtained according to the calculation error of the solution problem. This method can generate high-quality meshes, but does not require much expert knowledge.

articleTitle: The Design and Research Analysis of HVAC System Three-Phase Energy-Draining Fault Current Limiter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In high-voltage AC power grids, the DC component of short-circuit current can cause serious structural and functional damage to the power equipment. In this paper, the design and research anlyis of HVAC system Three-Phase Energy-Draining Fault Current Limiter (TDEDFCL) is proposed. And the accuracy and effectiveness of the structure of the TDEDFCL are proved by simulation.

articleTitle: A Novel Topology of an Axial Flux Type Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Due to rapid urbanization, urban air mobility (UAM) has been attracting considerable attention as a new mode of transportation. An electric vertical take off and landing (eVTOL), which is an aircraft for UAM, requires a motor with high specific power. Axial flux type motors have high specific power and high utilization of space. Meanwhile, the demagnetization of the permanent magnets reduces the output of the permanent magnet type motors and the supply of rare-earth elements is unstable. Therefore, a novel topology of an axial flux type wound rotor synchronous motor (AFWRSM) is proposed. In this paper, the structure and principle of the novel topology are described and design of the topology is carried out. Also, the electromagnetic characteristic of the proposed topology is analyzed by using the finite element analysis (FEA).

Author Keywords: electric vertical take off and landing

articleTitle: Study on the Rotor Bar Curvature to Increase Starting Torque in Cryogenic Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Induction motors in Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) pumps located inside LNG vessels operate submerged in -163°C LNG. Consequently, when the pump is not in use, components including bearings freeze, necessitating a design focus for cryogenic induction motors on achieving high starting torque over other aspects like efficiency. This paper has investigated the rotor bar design that maximizes starting torque in cryogenic environments for induction motors. Contrary to typical induction motors, it was found that in cryogenic conditions, the highest starting torque occurs where the front curvature of radius of the rotor bar is larger. This phenomenon is attributed to the greater influence of leakage inductance in cryogenic conditions compared to room temperature.

articleTitle: AC Iron Loss Investigation with Consideration of a DC Bias Magnetisation in Non-Grain Oriented Electrical Steel Sheets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This work deals with the characterisation and modelling of AC iron losses, of non grain oriented (NO) soft magnetic steel sheets, under the presence of a DC bias magnetisation. Such DC fields occur in multiple electrical motor topologies, e.g., permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSM), and lead to increased local iron losses, and therefore a greater demagnetisation risk of permanent magnets in use. Hence, this loss increase needs to be accounted for. In this paper numerous NO steel sheet samples are characterised and the influence of multiple parameters affecting losses is discussed. Furthermore, loss modelling approaches are presented and evaluated regarding their applicability in electric machine design.

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Model of Linear Induction Machine Considering Edge Effect and Core Saturation from Winding Function Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this article, the dynamic model of the linear induction machine (LIM) from the aspect of winding function theory has been investigated considering with the edge effect and core saturation. Firstly, the one-dimensional electromagnetic field model of LIM is established, and the primary and secondary windings are analyzed separately. Secondary, the electromagnetic performances such as thrust force have been derived based on the winding function theory. Then, the calculated performances have been evaluated and compared with the results analyzed by finite element analysis (FEA) method. Finally, the LIM has been tested, and the experimental results are consistent with the calculated results, which means that the established dynamic model can reflect the electromagnetic performance of the LIM. The research results have demonstrated the accuracy and validity.

articleTitle: Adaptive Mesh Refinement and Embedded Boundary Method for Streamer Discharge Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: We simulate streamer discharges in both two and three dimensions parallelly using an adaptive Cartesian mesh refinement and the embedded boundary method. A minimal fluid model is considered with a typical pin-plate domain. The embedded boundary method is taken to handle the curve boundary, and the adaptive mesh is introduced to reduce the number of degrees of freedom. Numerical experiments demonstrate the second-order convergence of the embedded boundary method and validate the efficiency of the adaptive mesh refinement. The effects of two different anode shapes are compared in three-dimensional streamer discharges.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Deep Learning for Topology Optimization of Permanent Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes the multiphysics deep learning to predict the characteristics such as average torque, torque ripple, maximum Mises stress and iron loss of a permanent magnet (PM) motor for topology optimization. The deep neural network is used as the surrogate model of time-consuming field computation to accelerate the topology optimization. This paper discusses the prediction accuracy of the motor characteristics, the optimization performance, and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Boundary Conditions in Magnetics: a Neural Network Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In the paper, the synthesis of boundary conditions in a doubly-connected domain is accomplished by means of a single-layer neural network. In this way, the classical problem of magnetic field continuation is solved utilizing innovative tools instead of classical regularization approach.

articleTitle: A Neural-Network Model for Helping the Synthesis of a Dual-Frequency Induction Heating Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In the paper an induction heating problem is considered. The Finite Element analysis is used to evaluate the temperature along a line on a graphite disk heated by a power inductor. Subsequently, a fully-connected Neural Network (NN) is trained with the aim of implementing a surrogate model able to compute the temperature profile on the disk, given the amplitude and frequency of the supply current.

articleTitle: Examination of Thickness Measurement Method for Hot Spring Scale inside Steel Pipes using Electromagnetic Force Vibration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: At geothermal power plants has a problem that the large-diameter steel pipe is blocked by solid material of hot spring water's components, called for “hot spring scale”. Therefore, it is necessary to develop a method for measuring the thickness of hot spring scale from the outside of large-diameter steel pipe. In this paper, we investigated a non-contact inspection method that uses electromagnetic force vibration to measure the thickness of hot spring scale from the outside of a steel pipe. In addition, the proposed inspection method was evaluated by comparing electromagnetic force and displacement analysis using the 3-D finite element method (FEM), and verification experiments.

articleTitle: A Study on the 2D Demagnetization Analysis Error Caused by the 3D End Effect in an Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In order to design of IPMSM, 2D finite element analysis is mainly used because of its short analysis time and low cost. The irreversible demagnetization of magnets in IPMSM is a very important performance characteristic. Therefore, accurate demagnetization analysis is essential for IPMSM design. However, demagnetization analysis of IPMSM cannot obtain accurate results with 2D FEA due to the 3D end effect caused by the fringing effect. In this paper, the causes of analysis errors that occur during the demagnetization analysis of IPMSM using 2D FEA were analyzed, and major design variables that strongly affect such analysis errors were identified.

articleTitle: Magnetodynamic and Thermal Homogenisation of Foil Windings for Magnetic Components
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This digest deals with the magnetodynamic and thermal homogenisation of foil windings for the magnetic components in power electronic converters. The electro-thermal design of magnetics requires accurate and fast power loss computation to guarantee the thermal constraints. Homogenisation techniques, either numerical or (semi-)analytical, usually handle both physics independently. In this work, we proposed a coupled approach for foil windings in high-frequency magnetic components.

articleTitle: Disturbance-Observer-Based Sliding Mode Speed Control for Variable Flux Memory Machines Considering Magnetization State Manipulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Variable flux memory machine (VFMM) requires injecting the d-axis current pulse to manipulate its magnetization state (MS) for permanent magnet (PM) flux linkage regulation, during which large speed fluctuations are usually caused. Therefore, this article proposes a disturbance-observer-based sliding mode speed control for VFMM drive systems to deal with their unique MS manipulation disturbances. A novel sliding mode speed controller (N-SMSC) considering both the normal operation and MS manipulation modes of VFMM is constructed to achieve better dynamic performance. Besides, the lumped disturbance, particularly the drastically changed MS manipulation disturbance, is estimated by a proposed new sliding mode torque observer (N-SMTO) combining with the model compensation, and then compensated into the speed controller. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method are validated through experiments.

articleTitle: High-Power and -Speed Induction Machines Iron Loss Calculation Incorporating the Electro-Thermal Impact
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper deals with the iron loss calculation and electro-thermal characterization of high-power and -speed induction machines (HSIM). In higher operating points, the iron loss may become increasingly higher as the frequency increases, and it necessitates meticulous consideration in machine design and analysis. The ever-higher frequencies and thermal limitation of components demand the fast and accurate power loss computation for an optimal design accounting for stringent electro-thermal limitations. To this aim and to circumvent the computational intensity of finite element analysis (FEA), an advanced analytical iron loss calculation method is developed for HSIM, wherein both magnetic and thermal field effects are concurrently considered. Prior works predominantly studied these aspects independently, while it is crucial to examine the interaction of these two strongly coupled physics in complex systems like HSIM. The developed model is showcased using a 94 kW, 14,000 r/min HSIM and validated FEA results. It demonstrated excellent accuracy across different operating conditions. This approach provides valuable insights for optimal design and performance improvement in HSIMs, with a focus on achieving a fast and accurate alternative to FEA that encompasses both electromagnetic and thermal factors.

articleTitle: Mechanical Field Calculation and Analysis of a High-Speed PMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The rotor system of high-speed permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM) needs to be carefully designed to ensure operational stability. In this paper, on the basis of the proposed 15kW, 120000 rpm High-Speed PMSM, the stress field of permanent magnet (PM) and sleeve are calculated and analyzed by using analytical method and finite element method (FEM), and relations between sleeve parameters and rotor stress are explored. Based on the sleeve scheme obtained, this study calculates the critical speed of rotor, and influence factors such as bearing stiffness and rotor structure are investigated.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Performance Analysis and Multi-Objective Optimal Design of A Novel Magnet-Shifted PM Motor for Reducing Torque Ripple
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In the manufacturing stage of permanent magnet motors, torque ripple is reduced through design. This article uses the Maxwell tensor method to explain the mechanism of reducing cogging torque, which will obtain the optimal magnet offset angle faster than finite element parameterization. The principle of harmonic generation is explained by calculating the winding factor of the motor. Due to the influence of various factors on the magnetic field, a multi-objective optimization strategy based on genetic algorithm and finite element calculation was chosen to obtain the optimal parameters.

articleTitle: A GPU Accelerated Semi-Implicit Method for Large-Scale Nonlinear Eddy-Current Problems Using Adaptive Time Step Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A transient magnetic vector potential formulation for nonlinear eddy-current problems and spatial finite-element discretization form a system of nonlinear algebraic diffential equations. Using a Rosenbrock-Wanner type time integration method, the system of nonlinear functions is solved with a series of linear systems of equations. For highly efficient simulations of large-scale problems, the process is accelerated using parallel computing and graphic processing units. An adaptive time step control is also used for ensuring the desired accuracy levels, without oversampling the time interval.

articleTitle: A New Hybrid Algorithm based on PSO and Fireworks Algorithm for Optimal Design of Metasurface Absorber in RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To tackle the nonlinear, multimodal, and computationally expensive challenges inherent in the optimal design of RF energy harvesters, an innovative hybrid algorithm combining particle swarm optimization and fireworks algorithm is proposed. In the proposed hybrid algorithm, 1) a stretching-and-ejection mechanism is developed to balance exploration and exploitation searches, 2) a self-adaptive inertia weight is introduced to enhance the convergence rate, 3) an elite- preservation strategy is employed to guarantee a global convergence. Also, a new topology of a wideband and dual-polarized metasurface absorber for RF energy harvesting applications is introduced. The feasibilities of the presented work in RFEH applications and design optimizations are validated using a case study.

articleTitle: A Prediction Model of Torque Control Parameters Considering Temperature-Dependency of IPMSM for High Speed Railway Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This study proposes a computationally efficient torque estimation model for interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM), considering the temperaturedependent magnetic property of a permanent magnet (PM). The proposed model considers nonlinear characteristics such as the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex> cross-coupling and saturation effect based on the flux linkage mapping with the least-square method. An IPMSM for traction application is used for the validation of the proposed method. The validity is verified with comparing the results between the proposed prediction model and the transient finite element analysis at different <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$PM$</tex> temperatures.

articleTitle: Effective Design Method of Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor for Electric Vehicle Using Initial State Finite Element Analysis and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel design methodology aimed at efficiently reducing the computation costs associated with axial flux permanent magnet synchronous motor (AFPMM). The proposed method is using analysis result of the initial position of the rotor called initial state finite element analysis (ISF) as a 3-dimensional analysis of AFPMM and generating a surrogate model using machine learning. This method can significantly reduce the computation time to analyze the nonlinear characteristics of the motor, as it does not perform any other periodic analysis. The performance of ISF will be verified through comparison with full periodic finite element analysis (FPF). And machine learning (ML) to be used for optimization of the proposed method is LightGBM, and performance verification will be made through comparison with other MLs in the test function. Through ISF, many samples generated at low computational costs will be combined with LightGBM to perform optimization, achieving many required performances of electric vehicle (EV) driving motors.

Author Keywords: Axial flux permanent magnet synchronous motor

articleTitle: Nonlinear MOR of Induction Motor with Reduced Representation of Airgap Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A model order reduction (MOR) of induction motor using the Cauer ladder network (CLN) method with reduced airgap-harmonic representation is parametrized to handle the magnetic saturation. The reduced harmonics set is fixed regardless of the variation in saturation level. The proposed method provides an efficient and accurate reduced model of an induction motor.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Dy-Free Permanent Magnet Motor for Irreversible Demagnetization through Experimental Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Recently, with global attention focused on environmental issues, major automakers have stopped producing cars with internal combustion engines. In contrast, production of electric vehicles has been gradually expanding. High-efficiency, high-power permanent magnet motors are essential for electric vehicles. These magnets are generally composed of rare earth materials, which raise concerns about future instability due to continuous price increases and supply challenges caused by national monopolies. In this paper, we propose a permanent magnet motor that does not use one of the rare earths, dysprosium (Dy). However, using permanent magnets without Dy lowers coercivity and lowers temperature characteristics, making them vulnerable to irreversible demagnetization. To address this issue, we modified the permanent magnet structure from bar-type to V-type, which is very vulnerable to external demagnetization factors. We then performed the optimization design using the Taguchi method, an experimental planning technique.

articleTitle: Estimation of Condition Number of Quasi-static Darwin Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper discusses the condition number of the Darwin model through a framework of a nearly singular system of equations, and the explicit expression of the frequency-dependent small singular values, which deteriorate the convergence rate of the iterative solver, is obtained.

articleTitle: A Stable Discontinuous Galerkin Time-Domain Method with Implicit-Explicit Time-Marching for Lossy Media
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: When the discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method with the explicit Runge-Kutta (RK) scheme is used to solve the electromagnetic problems involving lossy media, the solution is highly unstable and the time-step size is more strictly restricted. To overcome this bottleneck, we introduce the implicit-explicit RK (IMEX RK) method to the DGTD method, using the implicit RK scheme for the time marching of the conduction current term, while the explicit RK scheme for the rest, which can eliminate the instability caused by lossy media. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method breaks the limitation of the time-step size due to non-zero conductivity compared with the explicit RK method and preserves high-order accuracy.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Suppression in AC Motor Using Magnetic Periodic Reversal Spring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper designs a magnetic periodic reversal spring (MPRS) as a new method to suppress a torque ripple that inevitably occurs due to the operating principle of AC motors. The order, phase, and amplitude of the torque of MPRS attached to the output shaft of the interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) are optimally designed using magnetic field analysis software to suppress the torque ripple of IPMSM. As a result, the torque ripple could be reduced to about 53.8%.

articleTitle: A New Magnetic Design with Annular Sector Coils of an Inductive Angular Position Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: With the demands increasing of new energy vehicles, a new magnetic design with annular sector coils of an inductive angular position sensor with high accuracy and low cost was proposed to satisfy the assembling space requirements of vehicle. The proposed sensor was composed of a rotor mounted on the middle of shaft, an annular sector shaped excitation coil, and two relative receiving coils. The sensor was electromagnetically simulated by finite element method in transient analysis. The induced voltage was obtained through the simulation and processed to obtain the angle error. Prototypes will be manufactured and the simulated angular error will be experimentally verified.

articleTitle: Novel Design Optimization Strategy using a Lumped Magnetic-Circuit Model for Surface Permenet Magnet Machine with Step-skewing Rotor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel approximation strategy to three-dimensional(3-D) optimization design is proposed for surface permanent-magnet machines (SPMSM) with rotor overhang and step-skewing type motor using lumped magnetic circuit model. The rotor overhang method is applied to consider the tolerance of electric steel length in axial-direction and maintain the machine performances. The rotor step-skewing technique is used to reduce cogging torque, torque ripple value and THD of back-electro motive force (EMF). In general, the 3-D finite element method (FEM) analysis is requisite to analyze the performance of overhang and step-skewing SPM motor considering the additional flux on the overhang side and the leakage flux crossing section on the rotor magnet side. Moreover, to optimize the SPM topology for target performance, 3-D effect which are number of skew steps, shape of magnet and length of rotor, need to be considered. However, 3-D FEM optimization process requires abundant computation time and computing memory. To deal with this problem, main design variables is considered using lumped magnetic-circuit model. In addition, effective of this method is validated through comparison of 2-D, 3D and test results.

articleTitle: An Anisotropic Hysteresis Model Considering Microstructural Feature
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper introduces a physically-based anisotropic hysteresis model considering the microstructural features of non-oriented silicon steel. Drawing on the foundations of the Globus' model, the anisotropic anhysteretic curve is first deduced from the movement of the domain wall within individual grains. A static anisotropic hysteresis model is then proposed by considering the grain size related pinning field in the Energy-Based (EB) model to describe the irreversible displacement. The accuracy of the proposed model is validated through a detailed comparison with experimental data.

articleTitle: Analysis of Magnetic Field Modulation Mechanism in Transverse Flux Cylindrical Linear Generator Used in Direct Drive Wave Energy Conversion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Extracting wave energy for power generation is a decent way to meet sea area power supply demands. Among various power take-off devices, direct-drive wave energy converter (DDWEC) is more efficient in wave energy conversion. However, it still has demerits of low speed and low generator power density. Magnetic field modulation is a feasible method to increase speed and enhance power density. In this paper, a transverse flux cylindrical magnetic field modulated linear generator is proposed. The magnetic field modulation mechanism of this topology is elaborated. Different combinations of stator slots and translator poles are compared. The 12/11 topology proves to have a relatively low detent force (0.94N), thrust ripple (0.76%) and a high average thrust (247.01N).

articleTitle: Computation of Geometric Mean Distance through Monte Carlo Simulation to Predict Inductance of Circular Coil with Arbitrary Cross-Section
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The calculation of inductance is of paramount importance in various electromagnetic systems utilizing coils. Numerous research efforts have focused on calculating the self-inductance of coils, often providing formulas for approximating the inductance of coils with specific shapes. The self-inductance of a circular coil can be calculated directly using the geometric mean distance (GMD), but GMD calculations have rarely been studied except for simple cross-sections such as circles or squares. This paper introduces a method employing modified Monte Carlo simulation to obtain GMD based on the aspect ratio of arbitrary shapes. The proposed approach is applied to calculate the self-inductance of a circular coil with a complex cross-section.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Field Analysis Using Physics Informed Neural Net and Partial Differential Equation Solver Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The main novelty of using Physics Informed Neural Net (PINN) for electostatic field modeling is that it exploits the underlying physics law when training deep learning. This is attributed to the use of partial differential equations (PDE) as the loss function. Usually the loss function of PINN is implemented using automatic differentiation (AD). Inspired by a recent work known as the FDM-PINN [1], we propose to use PDE solver for implementing the loss function. In electrostatics field analysis, there are classical methods that try to solve PDE using numerical approach. Our goal is to complement the merit of classical PDE solver with modern PINN. In our experiment, we tested our PINN approach on a rectangular trough electrostatic field. We showed that our PDE solver based PINN consistently outperforms deep learning baselines in terms of error reduction.

articleTitle: Efficient Low-Frequency Human Exposure Assessment with the Maximum Entropy Snapshot Sampling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Reduced-order models of high-fidelity linear systems enable efficient and comprehensive numerical assessment of human exposure to low-frequency magnetic fields. These models are often generated by snapshot-based reduced basis methods, which rely on the singular value decomposition of a matrix whose columns are solution vectors of a high-fidelity system. However, most of these solution vectors provide redundant information, which turns the singular value decomposition into a computation-ally and memory-demanding step. With the maximum entropy snapshot sampling strategy, the number of solution vectors can be efficiently reduced to the essential ones. Therefore, this work aims to provide a reduced basis for human exposure assessment in a computationally and memory-efficient manner using this information-theoretic framework.

articleTitle: Effect of Building Modeling on Ion Flow Field of HVDC Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: 3D calculation and analysis for ion flow field is necessary to the residential houses adjacent to HVDC transmission lines. Traditionally, the corner of house is treated as sharp angle, leading to the singularity problem at the corner and affecting the calculation results near the corner. In this paper, a rounded corner modeling is applied to simulate the actual house corner. It shows that calculation results at rounded corners do not diverge and are little affected by the mesh size. New modeling method can improve calculation result around corner and has little effect on the results near the roof center.

articleTitle: Comparison of Electromagnetic Vibration and Noise of Sensorless Control with Pulsating Voltage Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: High frequency (HF) signal injection is the main method to achieve zero-low speed sensorless control of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). However, additional signal injection will generate additional voltage and current harmonic components and new air gap magnetic density and electromagnetic force wave components, leading to extra vibration and acoustic noise problems. In this paper, the new current harmonics, air gap magnetic density and electromagnetic force wave components generated by the pulsating signal injection sensorless control method are derived theoretically. The corresponding spatial order and frequency distribution are obtained. The simulation and experiment platform are built to underpin the validity of the theoretical analysis. By appropriately matching the injected signal frequency with the operating speed and motor modal frequency, the electromagnetic vibration and acoustic noise during motor operation can be significantly reduced.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Force and Vibration in Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors with Dynamic Eccentricity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Considering the current industrial machining accuracy limitation and installation error, the permanent magnet motor may have eccentricity problems, which will have a great impact on the radial electromagnetic force of the interior permanent magnet synchronous motor. In this paper, through the derivation of radial magnetic fields and electromagnetic forces in healthy and unhealthy (eccentric) states, it is found that the changes of electromagnetic force waves in time frequency and spatial order cause differences in vibration and noise. Finally, an 8-pole 36-slot interior V-shaped permanent magnet synchronous motor was taken as the research object, and the correctness of the theory was verified by formula derivation, numerical results, simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification for Electromagnetic and Thermal Characteristics of a High-Speed Permanent Magnet Motor with Two Different Rotors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This study presents an approach to calculating the temperature increase in the internal components of permanent magnet synchronous machines by improved electromagnetic loss analysis method. The effect of the electromagnetic wave characteristics according to the carrier harmonics on the electromagnetic wave loss of the motor is considered, and the thermal characteristics analysis method of the motor through the electromagnetic loss analysis method considering the magnetic field behavior is discussed. Finally, the validity of the thesis is presented through comparison with the experimental results, and a heat reduction design method through improved design is presented.

articleTitle: Improving Beam Commissioning by Fast Computation of Magnetic Field of Accelerator Magnets Considering Magnetic Hysteresis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In accelerator systems, fast magnetic field analysis incorporating the effect of magnetic hysteresis is essential for achieving high efficiency and accuracy in beam commissioning using electromagnets. In this paper, the fast magnetic field computation method with macroscopic play model is proposed. It is constructed by re-identifying the shape functions from the currents and magnetic multipole components characteristics obtained from a conventional finite element method incorporating the DC hysteresis effects. As a result of the examination, we verified that the proposed method accelerated the magnetic field computation, which was fast and accurate enough for beam commissioning.

articleTitle: Analysis on Conductive Screen Effects on Dual Air-Gap Surface Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: When double stator or double rotor configurations are used, electric motors with a double air-gap construction can achieve more power or torque density than their single air-gap counterparts. The authors of previous research suggested a double-stator permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) that isolated the inner and outer motors by placing a conductive screen in the center of the rotor. However, because the design was selected at random, the conductive screen analysis was not included in that study. The impacts of conductive screen size are the main topic of this study, which also determines the ideal dimensions for motor performance. A finite element analysis (FEM) is used to evaluate the screen's electroconductive properties. The motor is then produced and put to the test. According to the findings, there is a notable increase in efficiency when the size of the conductive screen is selected.

articleTitle: Model Order Reduction of Cage Induction Motor with Stator and Rotor Failures Based on Multiport Cauer Ladder Network Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This study investigates model order reduction for a cage induction motor with stator and rotor failures based on a multiport Cauer ladder network (CLN) method. First, three CLN methods are proposed, in which extracting dominant space harmonics in an air-gap flux density waveform and deriving circuit parameters in the CLN are performed differently. Then, the usefulness of the proposed methods is discussed in terms of calculation accuracy and calculation cost by comparing numerical results obtained by the CLN methods and a finite-element method.

articleTitle: Magnetostriction Model of Electrical Steel Sheet Considering Temperature Gradient
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In the magnetization process of certain high- temperature operational motors, it is common to observe non- uniform heat distribution, resulting in the formation of a temperature gradient. The existence of different temperature gradients will change the magnetostrictive properties of the electrical steel sheet (ESS), which will affect the vibration characteristics of the motor core. In this paper, a set of measuring platform for measuring magnetostrictive properties of ESS under the condition of temperature gradient is built. The dynamic magnetostrictive properties of ESS under different temperature gradients are measured and analyzed, and the anisotropic magnetostriction in different magnetization directions is explained. A model for evaluating the influence of different temperature gradients on magnetostriction of ESS is proposed to estimate the dynamic magnetostriction curve. Finally, the proposed model is verified by comparing the measured magnetostriction and computed one.

articleTitle: Homogenized-Winding Model of Inductor Considering Stray Capacitance at High Frequency for Finite Element Electromagnetic Filed Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In the inductors excited by the inverter using Gallium Nitride power devices, the ringing phenomenon, which occurs due to the multi-resonances during the short rise and fall time, increases noise and loss. The multi-resonances of the ring core inductor at high frequency (HF) can be represented by using the electromagnetic field finite element analysis (FEA) considering the stray capacitance of the winding in the frequency domain. However, it requires fine subdivision and expensive computation cost to consider the real structure of the winding in the FEA. To reduce the computation cost, a homogenized-winding model of the ring core inductor, in which one turn of wire with gap is represented by one element with equivalent conductivity and permittivity, is proposed and verified in this paper. It is shown that the HF characteristics of the ring core inductor obtained from the proposed homogenized-winding model are in good agreement with those obtained from the real-winding model with significantly reduced computation cost.

articleTitle: Using Point Clouds for Material Properties Smoothing in Low-Frequency Numerical Dosimetry Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Numerical dosimetry simulations are used to determine the electric field induced in the human body by low-frequency external magnetic fields. These simulations require a discretization of the human body to resolve the different tissues. Human models discretized with structured meshes are commonly prone to staircase errors at tissue interfaces caused by large gradients in the material properties. This paper presents an approach using point clouds to create mixed material fillings from existing voxel models to reduce the error in numerical simulations. A simplified head model for which analytical solutions exist can be used to quantify these errors. The error is reduced to a few percent if the structured mesh allows mixed material fillings.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Finite Element Method and High-Order Isogeometric Analysis for Modeling Magnetic Vector Hysteresis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This work presents a comparison between the finite element method and isogeometric analysis, when solving an electromagnetic problem with an included hysteresis model, for a high and low number of degrees of freedom respectively. The two methods are compared in terms of computational burden, i.e. time investment, for different refinement levels. Calculating the hysteresis effect is already taxing for two a dimensional problem, and even more so for three dimensions, up to the point where it can become impractical. Therefore, reducing the problem complexity is necessary to keep the valuable insight in machine performance, while also retaining practicality.

articleTitle: Analysis of A Linear-Rotary Generator With Magnetic Gears for Wave Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of low power density of low-speed direct-drive linear wave generators, a linear-rotary generator structure with a magnetic gear speed-increasing effect is proposed in this paper. The low-speed linear motion is converted into high-speed rotary motion through the magnetic gear screw. A double-stator axial flux generator and a magnetic gear form a composite generator structure. The rotor speed is further increased. The working principle of the generator is described. The electromagnetic properties of the generator such as magnetic density and static torque are analyzed. The generator proposed in this paper can adjust the wave capture capability according to the real-time size of the wave to achieve maximum power capture.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Force Analysis of Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors With T-Shaped Notching Rotor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper analyses the electromagnetic force(EMF) waves of a permanent magnet synchronous motor with T-shaped slots in the rotor. The analytical expressions for the EMF waves of the proposed motor are firstly derived from the theoretical aspects. And then the correctness of the theory and the ability of the scheme to effectively reduce the electromagnetic vibration of the motor are verified by means of finite element simulation calculation. In addition, prototypes were built and verified with relevant experiments.

articleTitle: Machine Learning to Predict Effective Conductivity of Composite Materials for Shielding Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The design of shielding systems such as enclosures for embedded electronics is often based on numerical modelling. When composite materials are used in these shields, it's necessary to determine their effective properties of equivalent homogeneous materials to simplify the modelling work. This paper presents an approach based on machine learning techniques to evaluate the effective conductivity of composite materials from measurements of their shielding effectiveness. Several composite samples are tested. The results obtained are validated by comparing the computed shielding effectiveness of the equivalent homogeneous materials to that obtained from measurements.

articleTitle: Inductance Derivation and Experimental Verification According to Operating Range of Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a method for deriving the inductance of an interior permanent-magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) by considering magnetic saturation. To obtain accurate inductance values during the motor characteristic analysis, it is necessary to consider the influence of core saturation on the magnetic flux changes. First, two distinct inductance calculation methods are presented, which are used to derive an inductance map across all operational regions. The torque was calculated using the derived inductance values. Finally, a comparison is made with the measurement results of the manufactured IPMSM.

articleTitle: An Improved Time Period FEM for Numerical Analysis of Electromagnetic Fields of Power Transformers under DC Bias
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The DC bias of a power transformer will increase the noise level and additional losses of the transformer. It thus is essential to calculate the transient electromagnetic fields of a power transformer under DC Bias. In this respect, the time period finite element method (TPFEM) is a feasible solution. However, the standard constant time step TPFEM will encounter deficiencies in solving a field problem with a sharp change occurring in a relatively small interval. To address this issue and improve the convergence, an improved adaptive time step TPFEM is proposed and validated in this paper.

articleTitle: Study on Transformer Core Vibration Noise Based on Low-Noise Electrical Steel Sheets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This study investigates the vibration noise of a single-phase four-column transformer iron core based on low noise electrical steel sheets. Firstly, electromagnetic performance tests were conducted on three types of electrical steel sheets, obtaining the hysteresis curve and magnetostriction curve. Subsequently, a model of a single-phase four-column transformer was established, and the acquired data were incorporated into a finite element method simulation model. This resulted in transformer magnetic flux density contour maps, vibration displacement diagrams, and noise levels based on the electromagnetic performance data of the three types of electrical steel sheets. Finally, vibration noise tests were performed on the physical transformer in the simulation model, obtaining the vibration noise values of the transformer iron core under operating conditions. A comparison was made between the experimental values and the simulation results, demonstrating the correctness of the simulation. By comparing experimental and simulation results, it can be inferred that the simulation calculations are accurate. The study on low-noise electrical steel sheets can provide support for the electromagnetic design, vibration reduction, and noise reduction aspects of transformers.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Partial Discharge on Multi-Dielectric Insulator Forming Migration-Ohmic Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Partial discharge characteristics were analyzed on a multi-dielectric insulator in air forming a migration-ohmic model by using fully coupled finite element method. In a HVDC or MVDC system, the electric stress is constantly applied to multi-dielectric insulators resulting in the movement of space or surface charge density. The concentration of surface charge density can cause the partial discharge problem which degrades the breakdown strength of the insulators. To consider an aging effect for dielectric insulators, the conductivity can be a good choice, but it is rarely reported to analyze this migration-ohmic model in discharge analysis. We, therefore, introduced the current continuity equation incorporating with the space charge continuity equations for electron, and positive and negative ions. To verify our numerical setup, we will compare the temporal surface charge decay on the surface of lossy dielectric insulator, obtained from an experiment through the surface charge decay (SPD) measurement with the Kelvin probe.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Novel Multiple Magnetic Source Axial Flux Modulation Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel multiple magnetic source axial flux modulation machine (MMS-AFMM) is proposed and investigated. Based on the dual modulation principle, four sets of magnets can be mounted on the stator and rotor. The topology of multiple magnetic sources enhances torque density and reliability. Six machines with different slot-pole combinations are presented and compared. The torque density of the MMS-AFMM reaches 15 Nm/kg.

articleTitle: Use of an Inference Technique for Sensitivity Analysis of RL Parameters of Wound Inductors Extracted from the Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this work, we compute the sensitivity of wound inductors RL parameters extracted using the Finite Element (FE) method with respect to geometric and material uncertainties, along a wide range of frequencies (from DC to 1 MHz). To that end, we compute the Sobol indices associated to a Polynomial Chaos Expansion based surrogate model of the uncertain FE model thanks to Bayesian inference technique.

articleTitle: Analysis of A Field Modulation Multi-Port Generator for Wave Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of low generator power density and unstable power capture caused by low wave speed and frequent wave speed changes, a field modulation multiport generator is proposed. Through the electric excitation magnetic gear, not only the rotation speed and power density of the generator are increased, but the maximum wave power capture capability of the generator can also be adjusted according to the real-time wave speed. The magnetic density distribution, static torque and back EMF of the generator are calculated and analyzed. The rationality of the designed generator structure was verified.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Axial and Radial Flux Motors with Identical Size and Output Power
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper offers a comprehensive comparative study of uniquely designed axial and radial flux motors with identical sizes and outputs. The primary objective is to analyze and contrast their design efficiencies, power densities, and loss characteristics under similar operational conditions. Using finite element analysis (FEA), this paper studies the differences between each motor type, focusing on important aspects such as magnet area, coil fill factor and electromagnetic losses. A key finding is that despite structural differences, both motor types demonstrate comparable power densities and efficiencies, each with distinct advantages and disadvantages. The full paper will include empirical validation through the manufacturing and testing of actual motors, aiming to provide a comprehensive understanding of axial flux motors and insights into design considerations with a focus on manufacturability.

articleTitle: Dynamic Multi-physical Field Coupling Analysis for Enhanced Electromagnetic Driving Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In order to solve the dynamic multi-physical field coupling problem in the working process of electromagnetic drive devices, a three-dimensional dynamic electromagnetic-heat-force coupling model is proposed. The dynamic distribution of current density, temperature and stress on the armature and rail during the driving process is analyzed. The results show that the current density, magnetic induction intensity and temperature are concentrated in the armature throat and the contact part between the armature and rail. And the Lorentz force is mainly concentrated in the armature throat. This model provides an important reference and guidance for the further optimized design of enhanced electromagnetic drive devices.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis of a Novel Arc Linear Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents the dynamic analysis of a novel design of an Arc linear permanent magnet synchronous motor. A special structure of an Arc linear permanent magnet synchronous motor having magnetically separated stator cores is analyzed and the results are presented in this paper. The performance parameters such as Back EMF, cogging torque, thrust force, and supply voltages are analyzed using 3D finite element analysis.

articleTitle: An Improved Thermodynamic Hysteresis Model for Electrical Steel Using Minimum of Magnetic Domain Energy to Compute Anhysteresis Magnetization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The thermodynamic model describes the hysteresis characteristics of electrical steel by analogizing the pinning point to dry friction, and the calculation efficiency is relatively high. However, the lack of a physical mechanism in the anhysteresis part results in limited accuracy of the model. The magnetic domain energy model can directly reflect the state of internal magnetic domains in the magnetization process of electrical steel, but the calculation course is complex and hard to engineering application. This paper combines the thermodynamic model with the magnetic domain energy model and proposes an improved thermodynamic model. Compared with the original model, this model not only retains the original model's calculation speed but also improves the calculation accuracy.

articleTitle: Accelerating Coil Path Optimization via Truncated Singular Value Decomposition Coupled with Adaptive Cross-Approximation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this study, we demonstrate improved speed in coil path optimization through the implementation of truncated singular value decomposition augmented with adaptive cross-approximation. The stream function method, which uses the normal component of the current vector potential as an unknown, is known to be a promising method for coil path optimization problems. The optimal coil path can be obtained by placing coils along the contour lines of the stream function. The truncated singular value decomposition method has been proposed as one of the methods to obtain the pseudo-inverse of the singular Biot-Savart kernels. However, the optimization of the three-dimensional coil path, i.e., the design of nuclear fusion reactor coils, requires an inexpensive method because the singular value decomposition is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(N.M2)$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(N, M)$</tex> is the size of the discretized Biot-Savart matrix. Therefore, we have proposed a method to reduce the memory usage and speed up and the truncated singular value decomposition by coupling it with adaptive cross-approximation and demonstrated its usefulness through numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Error Estimation of the Cauer Ladder Network Method for the Time-Domain Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The Cauer ladder network (CLN) method can speed up the eddy-current field analysis of electric machines in the time domain. A method for estimating the error and determining the order of the reduced model, i.e., the number of stages, is required. This study extends the estimation method in the frequency domain developed in a previous study to the time-domain analysis.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Design Approach to Minimize Position Error in Variable Reluctance Resolvers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In variable reluctance (VR) resolvers, harmonic components in the induced voltage across the secondary windings are critical to the accuracy of position sensing. Reducing inaccuracy requires precise design of stator windings, sensor geometry, and configurations. To reduce angle errors in VR resolvers, a systematic design method is presented in this paper. Finite element analysis (FEA) is used to examine the effects of changes in the stator windings, rotor surface geometry, and stator core geometry. Finally, an efficient design process is introduced that can minimize position errors using a genetic algorithm-based optimization algorithm.

articleTitle: Anisotropic 3D Thermal Modeling for a Racetrack Foil Coil
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Accurate thermal modeling of winding temperature is a key issue in the cooling system design of permanent magnet synchronous linear motors (PMSLMs). With the increasing demand on improving power density, foil conductors have become a choice in winding racetrack coils to ensure a superior thermal performance. However, one of the main obstacles in accurately modeling the racetrack coils is accounting for their anisotropic thermal conductivity. In this paper, two anisotropic modeling approaches based on finite element (FE) and thermal equivalent circuit (TEC) have been proposed, considering anisotropic thermal conductivity and bent geometry of a racetrack foil coil. Position-dependent thermal conductivity for the bent part of the racetrack has been derived. Heat conduction partial differential equations (PDEs) in both Cartesian and Cylindrical coordinates are solved to determine the equivalent thermal resistances considering anisotropy. To verify the approaches, the results contrasted with a multi-layer FE model and a homogenization FE model are discussed.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Linear Haptic Motor with Pure Magnetic Spring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: With a growing demand for haptic motors characterized by extended lifespan and superior performance, this paper introduces two innovative motor designs incorporating a pure magnetic spring. Employing the Maxwell stress tensor and an electromagnetic-mechanical coupling method, the force profile and acceleration results are analyzed, respectively. In the analysis of the link-type motor, the combined effects of x- and z-cogging forces on the mechanical system owing to its swing motion are considered. Notably, the link-type motor, showcasing comparable results to the prototype, emerges as a more competitive design.

articleTitle: A Study on Shaft Voltage of IPMSM Applying Tapering for Reducing Cogging Torque
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To mitigate cogging torque, a primary source of vibration and noise in the interior permanent magnet synchronous motors (IPMSM), the method of tapering to the rotor or stator is widely adopted. However, in the case of IPMSM applying a tapering model, the distance between the rotor-stator and coil-rotor varies. These variations have a significantly impact on the parasitic capacitance, the main factor in shaft voltage. Therefore, in this paper, the parasitic capacitance and the shaft voltage are analyzed when the tapering is applied to the rotor and stator. The electrostatic finite element analysis (FEA) is performed to obtain the parasitic capacitance of the tapering models. Then, the shaft voltage is verified by comparing the three prototypes (basic model, rotor tapering model, and stator tapering model) through the experiment.

articleTitle: Inductance Computation Acceleration with Fast Multipole Method for PEEC Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: High-temperature superconducting (HTS) magnets have been developed and studied for various ultrahigh-field applications worldwide. Rare-earth barium copper oxide (REBCO), known as a second-generation HTS, shows high performances even in a high field. To investigate the REBCO magnet behaviors, the partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) model is widely used. A great number of partial elements are required to simulate local phenomena. It takes a long time to compute the local mutual inductances in advance. In this paper, the concept of fast multipole method (FMM) is introduced as a first step toward fast computation of PEEC model simulation. The inductance computation time can be reduced by approximately 55% applying the FMM.

articleTitle: Analysis of Fire Propagation in Electrical Cable Tray Using the FLASH-CAT Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this study, a numerical method for fire modeling of electrical cable tray fires was developed for the purpose of improving fire safety in Nuclear Power Plants (NPPs). The simulation model was selected from cable fire experiments conducted under open atmosphere and enclosed compartment conditions from the fire propagation in elementary multi-compartment scenarios (PRISME) campaign, an international cooperative project of the Nuclear Energy Agency (NEA) of OECD. To solve the computational fluid dynamics problem of heat and smoke flow caused by fire, a numerical solution is obtained based on the Naver-Stoke's equation, which is suitable for low-speed heat flow. The governing equations consist of the mass, momentum, and energy conservation equations of the fluid and the ideal state equation as the governing equations, and the heat release rate per unit area, fire duration, and physical properties of the cable are considered as boundary conditions to perform the cable fire simulation analysis. The heat release rate curve for cable fires was assumed to be the FLASH-CAT model presented in NUREG/CR-7010. Based on the experimental results of cable fire scenarios, we developed a fire modeling procedure and applied various cable fire models to successfully develop an analysis method that is in good agreement with the experimental results.

articleTitle: Convolutional Physics- Informed Neural Networks for Fast Prediction of Core Losses in Axisymmetric Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: We adapt a convolutional approach on Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for solving the magnetostatic Maxwell's Equation on parametric axisymmetric transformer geometries. The trained PINN is capable of solving the physical equations in a matter of milliseconds for arbitrary geometries constrained by a total of 18 degrees of freedom (DoF). The results are analysed with respect to a numerical reference solution based on derived inductances and squared magnetic flux densities as an indication for resulting core losses. The combination of inference speed and accuracy enables new orders of magnitude for the optimization of transformer designs going forward.
