articleTitle: Design and Research on Machine Modulation Ratio Effect for Power Factor Characteristics of the Permanent Magnet Linear Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper investigates the power factor (PF) characteristics of the permanent magnet linear machine (PMLM) with the modulation ratio effect (MRE). Due to the machine MRE, the PMLM has more effective harmonics for the thrust force production, but it also has lower PF value. To investigate the relationship between the PF and MRE, the modulation ratio kmr is defined and the PF is also theoretically evaluated. Then, eight models with various combinations of slot and pole have been compared and evaluated. Finally, both the 12-slot/10-pole and 12-slot/14-pole combinations have lower kmr and higher PF, and the research results have validated the feasibility of the proposed method, which provides an approach in the PF optimization design.

articleTitle: An Implementation Method of Incorporating Hysteretic Material Models into Electromagnetic FEA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Hysteresis, as most important and intrinsic property of magnetic materials, however, is usually neglected in numerical analysis of electrical equipment due to its complicated history-dependent multi-valued nonlinearity, which will lead to inaccurate predictions of magnetic fields distribution and core loss. In this paper, an efficient implementation method of incorporating hysteretic material models into electromagnetic analysis is presented resorting to a commercial FEA package. This method is characterized by strong universality, and can be easily applied to other complex magnetic property models regarding anisotropy or hysteresis.

articleTitle: Effective Material and Static Magnetic Field for the 2D/1D-Problem of Laminated Electrical Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To simplify the design of electrical machines, often only one slice is considered instead of the entire machine. We propose a method, where the basic eddy current problem of a single iron sheet of laminated cores is investigated by a static magnetic field problem with an effective material in a 2D finite element model. The effective material is obtained by solving different suitable cell problems. Losses and reactive powers are assumed to be the same in cell problems. Voltage excitation is considered, i.e. the finite element model is coupled with an external circuit. The method with an effective material is very efficient and accurate as shown by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Study on Performance Changes of EV Traction Motor Applying CFRP Sleeve to IPMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In general, interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) is mainly used as the traction motor of electric vehicles. IPMSM uses a rib and bridge structure to prevent permanent magnets from being separated by centrifugal force when the motor rotates. Increasing the thickness of the ribs and bridges to satisfy rigidity at high speeds acts as a cause of increased leakage flux, thereby reducing motor performance. In this paper, to improve the performance of IPMSM, we benchmark existing products to derive a proto analysis model and verify it through testing. In addition, the rib and bridge shapes that cause leakage flux are removed from the proto model and a CFRP sleeve is applied. Next, stress analysis is performed to confirm whether the safety factor is met at the required maximum speed. And, as a result of comparing the no-load characteristics, it was confirmed that the leakage flux decreased and the back electromotive force (Back-EMF) increased. However, in the case of the CFRP model with increased Back-EMF, the current for field weakening control increases, making it difficult to drive at high speed. Therefore, amounts of permanent magnet used was reduced to bring the field weakening current to the same level as the proto model. Nevertheless, the CFRP model showed similar performance at the same output as the proto model.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Simulation and Measurement of MMC Submodule Under Dual Pulse Test
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Modular multilevel converter(MMC) is widely applied to the UHVDC power transmission system for its advantages of bidirectional power transmission, power qualities, and flexible controls. With a large number of insulated gate bipolar transistors(IGBTs) utilized in MMC converter stations, an extremely complicated electromagnetic environment is generated due to the dv/dt and di/dt during the IGBT switching process. A finite element method(FEM) is adopted to calculate the dual pulse magnetic field generated by the 4.5kV/5kA IGBT MMC submodule during the dual pulse testing process. Then, a dual pulse test is conducted and the pulse magnetic field is measured to verify the simulation result. Finally, a fast Fourier transform (FFT) analysis is performed to give a comprehensive view of the switching process and its mechanism as an electromagnetic interference source.

articleTitle: A Technique for Predicting Magnetic Field Signal of Warship by Applying Spatial Permeability to Reduce Computational Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In order to more simply model the complex structure and internal equipment of a ship made of magnetic materials, this study propose an analysis model that applies a certain permeability to space instead of internal structures. To verify this model, the electromagnetic analysis results are compared with the results measured on an actual ship, and its validity was confirmed.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of PM-Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Machines Considering Rotor Structural Integrity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel design approach implemented in the rib geometry of a permanent magnet-assisted synchronous reluctance machine (PMA SynRM) to enhance the structural integrity of the rotor core. Both mechanical and electromagnetic aspects were considered to balance performance trade-offs. Rotor stress was evaluated using von Mises stress through finite element analysis. Simulation results substantiate the applicability of the proposed technique in mitigating the stress concentration effect in the rotor core. This enables seamless high-speed operation without compromising the output torque.

articleTitle: Multiscale Thin Shell Finite Element Model for Mn-Zn Ferrites with Realistic Grain Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel approach is presented for high-frequency electromagnetic modeling of Mn-Zn ferrites while considering their realistic heterogeneous microstructure. The proposed approach is based on a multiscale finite element model utilizing thin shell elements for virtually discretizing the boundaries. The realistic microstructure is considered in the sense that the mesocell geometry has a grain-size distribution similar to one obtained from a microscope image. For validation, a ferrite core placed in a dielectric setting is modeled and its dielectric impedance is compared to measurements.

articleTitle: Improving Electrically Evoked Compound Action Potential Based on Electrical Field Imaging and Electrode Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The electrically evoked compound action potential (ECAP) has been used in various clinical studies and has become a key physiological signal for cochlear implants (CI). This study used four sensing electrodes to record ECAP signals based on the alternating polarity approach. An electrical field imaging (EFI) result based on the finite element method was used to obtain the interface impedance, then ECAP simulation results were computed and compared with a patient's clinical ECAP measurements. Preliminary modeling results show that the interface impedance obtained by this EFI-based technique can improve the simulation accuracy of the ECAP model. The ECAP modeling result will be compared with clinical ECAP measurements to validate the model in the full paper.

articleTitle: Fuel Cell Stack Magnetic Tomography with Adjoint Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To diagnose Fuel Cell stacks (FC-stacks) and aug-ment their durability, this paper presents a novel approach with an inverse algorithm based on magnetic tomography. The goal is to determine internal local resistivities of the stack from external magnetic measurements in order to provide a diagnosis. The inverse problem is solved by minimizing the difference between simulated and measured magnetic field. Sensitivities are computed with the adjoint state method and first numerical results are presented.

articleTitle: Fast Calculation of Shielding Effectiveness in Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a fast analytical procedure to evaluate the shielding effectiveness (SE) of conductive shields in wireless power transfer (WPT) systems. The methodology exploits the current image method combined with a compact SE calculation formulation, which can also be extended to multilayered shields. A standard case study is considered, and the results are validated through finite-element method (FEM) simulations.

articleTitle: Scattering Invariant Mode Wave Propagation in 3D Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This study examines low-loss microwave propagation in random media represented by 3D agroforest models. Low-loss propagation is achieved by creating scattering invariant mode (SIM) using antenna-beam forming, which is less affected by the statistical variation of the media than the regular beams used in radio wave communication techniques. The SIMs are calculated by the 3D numerical analysis of the forest. A hybrid method based on numerical calculations and the Foldy-Lax approximation is used to obtain fast results in the numerical analysis of the computationally large 3D problem. This approach makes it possible to create numerous results for building statistics for sensitivity analysis. The robustness of the Scattering Invariant Modes is examined by varying the geometry of the vegetation model.

articleTitle: Efficient Electric Field Evaluation of a Point Source Near the Infant Torso
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The key aim of this paper is the development of a simple and computationally affordable non-spherical model of the infant torso for the accurate calculation of the electric field from a nearby-located external point source. The new model consists of a multilayered host sphere containing four spherical inclusions for the representation of the different tissue group. The electric field is then determined via simulations for a Hertz dipole at 2.4 GHz substantiating the merits of the model's simplicity. Furthermore, since the model comprises simple structures (i.e. spherical bodies), the electric field can be accurately derived via dyadic Green's functions and the superposition principle for the appropriate surface boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Higher-Order Frequency Derivatives of Electroquasistatic System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Frequency sensitivity analysis (FSA) aimed to evaluate the reaction of electromagnetic field with respect to frequency variation. This study proposed a higher-order FSA of electroquasistatic (EQS) system. A variational formulation for the first-order FSA was obtained by differentiating a time-harmonic EQS system with respect to angular frequency. The higher-order formulation was sequentially derived from the lower-order formulation by repeating the differentiation. A continuum approach was taken so that the frequency sensitivity was expressed in an analytical form. Since the frequency sensitivity was evaluated prior to the discretization process of the finite element method (FEM), it could be readily and accurately calculated using commercial FEM software. The theoretical validity and numerical feasibility of this study were demonstrated in two examples.

articleTitle: Complete Characterization of EMI for ECMs with PEEC Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The method of partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) is employed to characterize the electronically commuted motor (ECM) systems by incorporating the parasitic effects of power traces in the PCB layout. The PEEC method is used to identify PCB parasitics in the electronic controller of ECM using Method of Moment (MoM) based electromagnetic simulator, ANSYS Q3D. The performance of the complete electronic controller system is simulated by including these parasitics in the controller circuit using Ansys Simplorer. It is confirmed that parasitics in the PCB layout contribute to voltage overshoot on the power device during regular switching operations and particularly during transient conditions such as output short-circuit. The simulation results are subsequently optimized to comply with FCC's Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) limits. The system is then measured for Common Mode (CM) and Differential Mode (DM) noise for EMI and results are compared with the simulated results, with agreement verified.

articleTitle: Physics-Informed Conditional Generative Adversarial Network for Inverse Electromagnetic Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In the quest to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of conventional sizing systems, this paper introduces an innovative machine learning-based approach leveraging Physics-Informed Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (PIC-GANs). By incorporating simple and cost-effective physical constraints, a magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC), into the learning process, our model not only adheres to realistic data generation but also aligns with underlying physical principles, offering a more robust and versatile solution, and tailored to specific conditions with lower computational expenses than traditional methods. This approach is adopted for use in the preliminary design stages of a linear actuator in magnetostatics.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network Based Electro-Thermal Optimization of Induction Machine for EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Prior studies have proposed various methods to mitigate the computational burden of design optimization in induction machines (IM) through finite element analysis (FEA). However, they often face high computational complexity, where the computation time increases significantly with the number of input parameters considered. Additionally, these methods mostly focus exclusively on the individual physics of IMs (electromagnetic or thermal aspect) without addressing their interdependent influences. To confront these issues, this study explores the utilization of artificial neural networks (ANN) for the IMs' design optimization, taking into account their Multiphysics aspects. The goal is to leverage ANNs power to efficiently tackle complex design optimization challenges while reducing computation time, thus simplifying achieving optimal electro-thermal performance. Through in-depth analysis and modeling, the research illuminates ANN's potential in developing superior designs, while also meeting speed and accuracy criteria. The findings introduce a novel approach that integrates advanced computational tools with traditional design methods to enhance IM performance across various applications with implications for other machine types.

articleTitle: Crack Propagation of Ground Insulation Failure for Large Motor End-Winding Based on Electromechanical Coupling Phase Field Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The ground insulation is a key component for large electrical machine, which may present the crack defect after the process treatment and assembly of manufacturing. In this paper, the crack propagations of the ground insulation failure with initial crack in stator end-winding of the large motor were studied by using the coupled phase field model. In the proposed model, the coupled effects of mechanical and electrical fields on the crack propagation and the evolutions were considered by using phase field method and finite element analysis. The results in this paper may provide a new way for the research of multi-factor damage diagnosis and life prediction of motor insulation coupling.

articleTitle: Design of Asymmetric Consequent-Pole SPMSM for Reduction Torque Ripple
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a design method is proposed to reduce a torque ripple and magnet usage in Consequent-Pole Surface Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor(CP-SPMSM). Based on the basic model of CP-SPMSM, it is analyzed that the model combining CP-Npole and CP-Spole can reduce torque ripple. Furthermore, the asymmetric pole arc ratio and position angle are designed considering torque and torque ripple. Finally, the axial asymmetric structure is proposed to reduce the torque ripple.

Author Keywords: consequent pole surface per-manent magnet synchronous motor(CP-SPMSM)

articleTitle: A Novel Multi-Layer Coupler with High Efficiency and High Misalignment Tolerance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) is a major preferred solution for charging technology due to its convenience and safety. However, the decrease in efficiency is often caused by problems such as misalignment. This paper designs a coupler with high efficiency and high misalignment tolerance. By simulation analysis and experimental prototype, the feasibility of the design scheme was verified.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Hybrid Excited Linear Machine with Characteristic of Air Gap Balanced
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The existing guiding technology of ropeless lifting system has the problem of difficult to ensure the air gap uniform during dynamic operation, which causes the vibration and noise between wheel and rail. To address this issue, a novel hybrid excited flux-reversal linear machine with characteristic of air gap balanced (HEFRLM-AGB) is proposed in this paper. Due to the space confliction between armature and field windings in conventional hybrid-excited machine, the partitioned primary structure with permanent magnet inset is employed to reduced flux leakage and enhance the power density, meanwhile, the two field windings are applied to flexible modulate the air gap magnetic field. Firstly, the topology, operation principle and flux regulation mechanism are introduced. Then, considering the complex magnetic path, the improved Taguchi multi-objective optimization method is used to obtain the optimal deterministic values. Finally, the machine design and optimization method are evaluated and verified by both finite element analysis and prototype experiments.

articleTitle: Semi-Implicit Time Integration Method for a FEM-Parameterized Plant Model of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A FEM-parameterized motor model considering the armature current- and rotor position-dependent characteristics is widely used in designing control systems of a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) as its plant model. However, it is indispensable to achieve further speedup for real-time simulation of the plant model. In this study, with a view to speeding up the circuit simulation by avoiding iterative calculations required to solve nonlinear equations, semi-implicit time integration methods are applied to the PMSM plant model, and the effectiveness of the presented approaches is verified.

articleTitle: Effect of Coil Shape on the Critical Load Resistance of Frequency Splitting Phenomenon in Magnetic Resonance Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The Frequency Splitting Phenomenon (FSP) is that the output power decreases rapidly at the resonant frequency, and the maximum output occurs at the other two frequencies when the transmission distance is closer than the conventional distance, or the load resistance is smaller than the conventional resistance. Therefore, the critical load resistance at which the FSP starts is an important factor to consider when designing a resonant coil. In this paper, the effect of resonant coil shape on the critical load resistance that causes FSP is analyzed.

articleTitle: Data-Efficient Machine Learning Methods for Electric Motor Surrogate Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Typical electric motor design process involves time-consuming finite-element simulations. In recent years, machine learning and deep learning techniques have been investigated for the development of surrogate models which provide rapid evaluation of motor designs. One drawback of these techniques is the requirement of large dataset in order to achieve reasonable prediction accuracy. In this paper, we present strategies in developing data-efficient machine learning and deep learning surrogate models for electric motors: reducing input dimensions, utilizing physics knowledge for hybrid models, and applying feature extraction methods using geometrical and topological data analysis tools.

articleTitle: Structural Parameters Optimization of Double Pendulum Damper Used in AC Transmission Lines Aiming at Reducing Corona Discharge Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To solve the corona discharge audible noise problem during the trial operation of an AC transmission line, first, the corona discharge location identification was completed with infrared imagery and ultraviolet imagery technologies. Then, through the three-dimensional electric field analysis about special transmission line fittings, three optimization schemes about double pendulum damper were checked preliminary. Thirdly, corona discharge tests at high voltage test site about the optimization schemes were accomplished and optimal radius of sphere-cylinder structure was selected combined with field operation requirements. Finally, the field reliability retests were completed and the result showed that the corona discharge noise of double pendulum damper was inhibited, the average sound pressure levels at noise sensitive area boundaries was 4.2 dB less than before and the acoustic environment quality along this transmission line was improved significantly.

articleTitle: Shape Optimization of Synchronous Motors for Torque Ripple Reduction Using Continuum Sensitivity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimization method for designing motor shape using a continuum sensitivity analysis to reduce torque ripples. An objective function was formulated as the weighted sum of energy differences corresponding to rotor position deviations, and the continuum sensitivity was derived using the concept of a material derivative. A design velocity to optimize the motor shape was calculated from the design sensitivity. To validate the proposed method, the shape design of the 4- pole synchronous reluctance motor was performed.

articleTitle: Notice or Removal: Conductor Design Method Considering AC Resistance for High Efficiency of PMSM using High Fill Factor Winding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Removed.

articleTitle: Nondestructive Inverse Estimation Method of Permanent Magnet Magnetization Using No-Load BEMF of PMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Because a magnetization process of permanent magnet (PM) with high accuracy is desirable for manufacturing a high-performance PM synchronous motor (PMSM), the PM magnetization estimation in the design process is essential. After the post-assembly magnetization of PM loaded on the PMSM, the no-load back electromotive force (no-load back EMF, hereafter abbreviated as BEMF) is utilized for the simple estimation of the magnetization condition of PM. However, since the estimation is performed by comparing the back EMF measured under the no- load condition with the reference PM, the PM magnetization is not directly estimated. In this study, the direct estimation method of PM magnetization using back EMF of PMSM is proposed.

articleTitle: Analytical Computation of Torque-Speed Characteristics and Efficiency Map for PM Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper provides an analytical solution for designing a Brushless Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (BLPMSM) to compute its torque-speed characteristics and associated efficiency map. This approach combines the torque-speed computational algorithm with analytical open-circuit PM flux computation followed by EMF and torque computations. The torque-speed algorithm uses the Ferrari method to compute torque in MTPA and flux weakening regions. Subsequently, the efficiency map can be calculated for the entire speed range. The proposed comprehensive analytical approach can be useful for design optimisation in terms of significantly reducing computational efforts. Finite element analysis (FEA) is used to validate the analytical results.

articleTitle: Computation of Movement Involved Eddy Current Field using Boundary Adaptation of Overlapping Mesh
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The calculation of eddy current field in the motional scenario is a difficult problem. Due to the movement of conductors, the original mesh may be largely deformed. For engineering models with complex shapes, it is time-consuming to re-mesh the mesh before each time step calculation. In order to avoid remeshing, this paper proposes a new calculation method based on overlapping non-conforming meshes. Without changing the topology of the background mesh, the invasion boundary is transformed into a non-conforming boundary between the elements, avoiding generating arbitrarily small or irregular cutting elements. Further, the mortar technique is used to deal with the field computation involving non-conforming boundary.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization of Magnetic Microstructures for Eddy Current Loss and Permeability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents the topology optimization of the microstructure of magnetic materials using the homogenization technique, seeking the maximum anisotropic and isotropic permeability and the lowest eddy current losses. The optimization results in the layered and particle-like structures for anisotropic and isotropic permeabilities, respectively.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Electromagnetic Characteristics of Permanent Magnet Linear Oscillating Actuators with different Laminated Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Tubular permanent magnet linear oscillatory actuators (TPMLOAs) are widely used in the compressor field due to its simple structure and high-power density. However, the traditional assembly method leads to the low lamination coefficient. Therefore, a hybrid lamination method is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the basic topology of TPMLOA is introduced, and the stator scheme using hybrid lamination mode is given. Then, taking the loss, the output thrust and processing cost as the target, the proportion coefficient of silicon steel sheet in the hybrid lamination mode is optimized. Finally, the electromagnetic characteristics of TPMLOAs with traditional lamination and hybrid lamination are compared and analyzed by three-dimensional finite element analysis (3-D FEA) considering the fabrication error. The comparison results show that hybrid lamination model can not only significantly improve the excitation thrust, but also effectively avoid fabrication error.

Author Keywords: Tubular permanent magnet linear oscillation actuator

articleTitle: Modal Analysis for Induced Currents in Metallic Plates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A number of electromagnetic systems and devices comprise metallic plates, acting either as a structural support to other, active parts of the system, or as an electromagnetic shield. In the case of external anomalous or unwanted electromagnetic solicitations, the plates are interested by induced currents. The currents couples with electrically active parts of the system, generating spurious effects. The computation of reaction fields and the coupling with the structures to correctly size the protection circuits is usually done numerically. In this study, we propose a modal analysis of the plate current map to achieve a semi-analytical expression, and we attempt to relate plate modes to a suitable set of lumped elements to be integrated within an equivalent circuit of the system active parts for the sizing of the protection system.

articleTitle: Study on High-Frequency Transformer with Variable Inductance for Extending the Maximum Power Level of DAB Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a method for using transformer variable inductance to extend the maximum power level of a dual active bridge (DAB) converter. The DAB converter is a solid-state transformer (SST) that requires high efficiency, power density, flexibility, and stability. Variable inductance makes it easier to achieve and extend maximum power levels. This paper presents a method for adjusting the inductance based on the core insertion conditions of the transformer used in the DAB converter without requiring an additional inductor. The proposed method is validated by analyzing the variable inductance characteristics of the transformer based on core insertion conditions and simulation results within the range of variable inductance.

articleTitle: Fixed-Point Cauer Ladder Network Method for Eddy-Current Problems with Hysteresis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: We present a novel nonlinear Cauer Ladder Net-work method based on the Fixed-Point technique for the anal-ysis of nonlinear eddy current problems. In the conventional nonlinear Cauer Ladder Network method, the circuit elements are parameterized, which means that the basis functions also change during the time evolution. This makes the method complicated. However, in the proposed method, the nonlinearity is concentrated on the right-hand side terms by using the Fixed-Point technique, so that the nonlinearity only appears in the controlled source terms connected to each stage. The voltage gains of the controlled sources are obtained by nonlinear iterations. We demonstrate the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method by applying it to numerical examples.

articleTitle: Mesh Error Estimation Using Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNN) can be applied to predict element error based on domain and mesh features. This approach allows for refinement typical of the Adaptive Finite Element Method (AFEM) without solving any meshes, only requiring an estimate-refine pattern and eliminating the need to solve at every iteration. In complex domains, the model is able to recognize subsections of the domain seen in training and use this knowledge to accurately predict element error across the entirety of an unseen mesh.

articleTitle: Application of POD to Time Domain Simulation of Nonlinear Field-Circuit Coupled Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) is applied to time domain simulation of a coupled magnetic field – electrical circuit problem under voltage excitation. To solve the nonlinear system equation when using the reduced order model (ROM), an interpolation technique combined with partial resampling is proposed. The interpolation model is constructed on the work point in each time step, which leads to a linear matrix. To evaluate the model reduction technique, the transient state of an E-core inductor is studied using the full finite-element model and the ROM.

articleTitle: Optimization Design of Surface Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor with Hybrid Magnets Using Analytical Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, the surface permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) which uses hybrid magnets to generate sinusoidal air-gap magnetic field is designed and analyzed. Additionally, an optimization based on analytical method is introduced, aimed at significantly reducing the motor's design cycle. Firstly, a fast analytical method is proposed for SPMSM with NdFeB and ferrite hybrid magnets. And the accuracy of the method is verified by comparing with the finite element method (FEM) results. Building upon the analytical model, a global optimization method is proposed, with torque ripple, output torque, and cogging torque considered as optimization objectives. The optimization focuses on tuning the polar arc coefficient of the magnet. Subsequently, FEM validations of the optimization model are conducted to affirm the effectiveness of the proposed design and optimization method. The results demonstrate the practical applicability and efficiency of the proposed analytical and optimization methods in enhancing the performance of SPMSMs.

articleTitle: The Analytical Calculation and Measurements of the Magnetic Force Between Permanent Magnet and Rotor Yoke of a Large-Scale Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents analytical calculations and measurements of the magnetic force between the permanent magnet (PM) and rotor yoke in a large-scale PM synchronous generator (PMSG). Assembling PM in a large-scale PMSG is challenging due to its significant magnetic force. Accurately predicting the PM magnetic force during assembly is crucial. The analytical solution provided in this paper is valuable for designing the PM assembly zig in various machine sizes. An experimental setup, scaled down and incorporating a steel plate to neutralize magnetic forces, is used. Results from experiments and analytical solutions are compared to validate the accuracy of the calculations.

articleTitle: A Magnetic Flux-Modulated Permanent Magnet Machine for Shaftless Pump-Jet Propulsor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a new magnetic flux-modulated permanent magnet (PM) machine (FPMM) for the shaftless pump-jet propulsor of the full electric ship system. The proposed FPMM embeds a reverse coaxial magnetic gear (CMG) into the interior of a high-speed PM machine to improve the torque density of the propulsion machine. A FPMM and a low-speed PM machine with the same technical parameters are designed. The corresponding torque performance, machine volume and mass are effectively evaluated using the finite-element method.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Impacts of Machine Parameter Mismatch on Sensorless PMSM Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, the dynamic performance and control stability of sliding mode observer (SMO) and model reference adaptive system (MRAS)-based sensorless drives are discussed under the machine parameter mismatch. The detailed theoretical analysis for the dynamic performance and control stability influenced by the parameter mismatch is conducted. The improved MRAS observed based scheme is proposed to solve the control instability issue. Both the simulation and experimental results verifies the control performance under parameter mismatch.

articleTitle: Time Signals Prediction from Electromagnetic Simulations of Lossy Devices Using LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Time-domain electromagnetic simulations of lossy devices that work in the frequency range of gigahertz or terahertz can be computationally costly since the mesh required by these equipment becomes extremely large. This work shows that this problem can be mitigated using recurrent neural networks. This architecture manages to grasp the time series dependence of the signal and extrapolates them after being trained with little data. Hence, the electromagnetic simulation in the time domain can be quickly estimated for later time samples.

articleTitle: Moving Mesh Method for Semiconductor Device Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: We propose a moving mesh method based on the harmonic mapping to numerically simulate the fundamental equations of two-dimensional semiconductors. The objective is to redistribute the mesh to the regions exhibiting large and sharp gradients in the numerical solution, thus achieving finer meshes in these areas. This approach leads to a reduction in the total number of meshes compared to traditional uniform meshes. In the case of multiple PN junctions, we divide the computational domain appropriately to ensure that each subdomain contains at most one PN junction. Furthermore, independent monitor functions can be employed in different subdomains. Numerical experiments demonstrate the efficacy of this method in automatically adjusting the mesh placement based on the gradient of physical quantities. Notably, this approach enables local refinement without altering the number of meshes.

articleTitle: Real-Time Design and Characterization of Inductive Position Sensors Through AI-Driven DesSS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: We propose a fast method to characterize inductive position sensors with zero physical prototypes. The technique is based on an in-house developed electromagnetic simulation tool which shows three orders of magnitude improvement with respect to the most widely used commercial software. This simulation software is used for producing synthetic data for training a machine learning surrogate model based on a neural network. In this way, the characterization of a sensor takes just milliseconds. This opens the possibility of devising a Design Support System (DesSS), a software that guide the user in sensor design for the best possible outcome, thereby saving development time.

articleTitle: A Design Method of Biplanar Uniform Field Coils Based on Magnetic Shielding Rooms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The digest presents a design method of biplanar coils to realize precise compensation for residual magnetic fields inside magnetic shielding rooms (MSR). The magnetic field generated by the biplanar coils inevitably couples with the magnetic shielding material, thereby deteriorating the uniformity of the magnetic field in the target region. Based on the coupling principle of the coils, the mirror image method is introduced into the traditional target field method. An improved particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is used to obtain the coils' parameters, thus determining the shapes of the coils. The simulation results show that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{B}_{x}$</tex> coil designed by this method can generate a more uniform magnetic field inside MSR.

articleTitle: Analytical Design and Optimization of Surface-Mounted PMSMs with Equal-Thickness Air Gap
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a method of analytical design and optimization for surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSMs) with equal-thickness air gap, which has better assembly accuracy and lower electrode inter-pole leakage. The outer surface of the permanent magnet (PM) is maintained as an arc shape, and the internal surface of the PM is designed and optimized to produce the sinusoidal air-gap flux density, which can reduce torque ripple. The thickness of the PM is derived considering the distortion of the air gap magnetic field by stator slots. In order to improve the average torque and reduce the torque ripple, the thickness of the PMs is further optimized by multiple harmonic injection using a genetic algorithm. Finally, the performance of three SPMSMs, namely, sinusoidal shape, shape considering stator slots, and shape by optimization, are compared.

articleTitle: Selection of Shared Rotors for Magnetic Geared Motor to Reduce Permanent Magent Usage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper introduces the design method for the shared rotor of a Magnetic Geared Motor (MGM). The MGM is a device that combines magnetic gears and a motor. Due to the substantial usage of permanent magnet, research has been conducted to reduce the amount of permanent magnet usage while maintaining the same output. The proposed method is applicable to the SPM type, and a phenomenon of reduced iron loss associated with the decrease in the core width of the shared rotor has been observed. Therefore, a comparison was conducted between an improved model with reduced core width and an IPM type, which minimizes iron loss. Through this comparison, the rotor configuration most suitable for the shared rotor of the magnetic geared motor was determined. The comparison models were analyzed using 2D-FEA.

articleTitle: 2-Step Monte Carlo Tree Search for Optimal Design of High-Frequency Toroidal Inductors in Power Electronics Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimization technique for toroidal inductors utilizing a 2-step Monte Carlo tree search. The approach combines a global search utilizing analytical formulas with a local search involving three-dimensional finite element analysis. Through the proposed method, optimal core materials, sizes, number of turns, and windings are determined to maximize the efficiency and minimize the size of the inductors. The proposed method is applied to the optimization of the inductors in a 6.78MHz electric-coupling power transfer system. The proposed method found the optimal inductor with low computational cost and the system measurement confirmed that the optimized inductor improves over 1.8% of the system efficiency compared to the previously designed inductor.

articleTitle: A Fast Calculation Method for Current-Carrying Capacity of Submarine Cables in J-Tube Sections
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Due to the enclosed air interlayer in the J-tube section, it has the potential to limit the current-carrying capacity of offshore wind farm export cables. The standard calculations outlined in the IEC guidelines are deemed inadequate for this unique laying method. Conducting fluid simulations can be time-consuming and challenging to implement in practical engineering scenarios. This article introduces a rapid calculation approach for determining the current-carrying capacity of submarine cables in J-tube sections, utilizing a semi-empirical correlation formula for natural convection in a vertical enclosed annular space and an axial heat transfer model for submarine cables. A comparative analysis between the proposed method and thermal-fluid coupling numerical simulations demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Multi-Physics Modeling for Thermal Interruption Capability Estimation of CO2/O2 Mixed Gas Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-physics model for the estimation of thermal interruption capability in a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> mixed gas circuit breaker (GCB). The ohmic loss of the insulation gas is calculated from the current continuity equation and utilized as a heat source for thermal fluid analysis. To accurately estimate the thermal interruption capability of a GCB adopting a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> mixture, we proposed a multi-physics model coupled with an electric model and a thermal fluid dynamics model. The validity of the proposed multi-physics model was verified by comparing it with experimental data. Subsequently, interruption indices were predicted using the calculated parameters to estimate the thermal interruption capability.

articleTitle: Transient Performance Characterization for a Shielded Rogowski Coil Based Low Power Current Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Rogowski coil (RC) based low power current transformer (LPCT) has been widely spread in smart substations for metering and protection applications. In this paper, the transient performance characterization is carried out for a shielded RC based LPCT. For this purpose, an equivalent lumped circuit model taking into account the effect of electrostatic shield screen is constructed and then the transfer function is derived. Experimental validation is conducted by considering the distortion current and faulty current signals.
